sentences.zh: 完顏撒改

translations.literal: Wanyan Sagai
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sagai

sentences.zh: 完顏撒改，上京納魯渾河人也，其先居於兀冷窟河。

translations.literal: Wanyan Sagai was a man of the Naruhun River in Shangjing; his ancestors had dwelt at the Ulengku River.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sagai was from the Naruhun River region of Shangjing; his forebears had lived along the Ulengku River.

sentences.zh: 身長多力，善用槍。

translations.literal: His body was tall and he possessed great strength; he was skilled in using the spear.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and powerfully built, he was an expert spearman.

sentences.zh: 王師南征，睿宗為右副元帥，置之麾下，佩以金牌，使督軍事。

translations.literal: When the imperial army marched south, Prince Rui served as Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief; Sagai was placed under his command, awarded a gold tablet, and charged with overseeing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign, Prince Rui held the post of deputy commander on the right; Sagai was assigned to his staff, given a gold command tablet, and put in charge of military operations.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，授本班祗候郎君詳穩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan, he was appointed Xiangwen of the Benban Qihou Langjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan, he was made xiangwen of the Benban Palace Attendant Corps.

sentences.zh: 其後從軍泰州路，軍帥以撒改為萬戶，領銀朮可等猛安，戍北邊，數有戰功。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed the army on the Taizhou Route; the army commander made Sagai a wanhu, leading the meng'an of Yinzhuke and others to garrison the northern border, with repeated military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned on the Taizhou Route, where the commander appointed him wanhu in command of the Yinzhuke meng'an and others to guard the northern frontier, winning distinction in battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 天德二年正月，海陵庶人遣使夏國，諭以即位事，因令伺彼之意。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiande, the Deposed Prince Hailing sent envoys to the Xia state to inform them of his accession and also ordered them to observe their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tiande 2, the deposed Emperor Hailing sent envoys to Western Xia to announce his enthronement and to sound out their reaction.

sentences.zh: 既還，稱旨，為尚書兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When he returned, his mission pleased the emperor, and he was made Langzhong in the Ministry of War of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the mission met with approval, and he was appointed a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 改同知會甯尹，遷迭剌部族節度使，改甌裏本群牧使，為曷懶路都總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Huining Prefecture, promoted to Military Commissioner of the Diela Tribal Division, changed to Commissioner of the Ouliben Pasturage, and made Chief Commander of the Yilan Route.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as vice prefect of Huining, became military commissioner of the Diela tribes, was reassigned to oversee the Ouliben pasturages, and finally was made chief commander of the Yilan Route.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，授衛州防禦使，為武震軍都總管。

translations.literal: When Hailing attacked Song, Sagai was appointed Defender of Weizhou and made Chief Commander of the Wuzhen Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Hailing's campaign against Song, he was made defender of Weizhou and chief commander of the Wuzhen Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣使召撒改，既至，除昌武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he sent envoys to summon Sagai; once he arrived, he was made Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong came to the throne, he summoned Sagai to court and appointed him military commissioner of the Changwu Army.

sentences.zh: 已而為山東路元帥副都統，改安化軍節度使，兼副都統如故。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Shandong Route, was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army, and retained his concurrent post as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named deputy commander-in-chief on the Shandong Route, then military commissioner of the Anhua Army while keeping his deputy command.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙鎮安武，仍兼副統。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to garrison Anwu, still holding the concurrent deputy command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was shifted to Anwu, retaining his post as deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 領山東、大名、東平三路軍八萬餘渡淮，會大軍伐宋。

translations.literal: He led more than eighty thousand troops of the Shandong, Daming, and Dongping routes across the Huai to join the main army in attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: He led over eighty thousand men from the Shandong, Daming, and Dongping commands across the Huai to unite with the main force against Song.

sentences.zh: 進至楚州，宋遣使奉歲幣。

translations.literal: Advancing to Chuzhou, Song sent envoys bearing the annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Chuzhou, Song dispatched envoys with the annual tribute payment.

sentences.zh: 還邳州，卒。

translations.literal: Returning to Pizhou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on his return to Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 龐迪，字仲由，延安人。

translations.literal: Pang Di, style name Zhongyou, was a man of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Di, whose style was Zhongyou, came from Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，喜讀兵書，習騎射，學推步孤虛之術，無所效用。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited; he delighted in reading military texts, practiced mounted archery, and studied the arts of calendrical calculation and divination, but found no use for them.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and unconventional, fond of military treatises and horsemanship; he also studied astrology and divination, though these skills never served him.

sentences.zh: 應募，隸涇原路第三副將，破賊有功，授保義郎。

translations.literal: He answered a recruitment call, was attached to the third deputy commander of the Jingyuan Route, achieved merit in defeating bandits, and was awarded the rank of Baoyi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted and served under the third deputy commander on the Jingyuan Route; after distinguished service against bandits he received the rank of Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 嘗從百餘騎經行山谷，遇夏人數千，眾皆駭懼請避，迪遂躍馬犯陣，敵皆披靡，身被重創，神色自若，完軍以還。

translations.literal: Once, leading a little over a hundred horsemen through a mountain valley, he encountered several thousand Xia troops; all were terrified and asked to withdraw, but Di leaped his horse into the enemy formation; the foe scattered before him; though he suffered grave wounds, his bearing remained composed, and he brought the whole force back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding through a mountain pass with a little over a hundred men, he met several thousand Western Xia troops. His companions panicked and urged retreat, but Di charged straight into the enemy line. The Xia ranks broke before him. Though badly wounded, he kept his composure and brought every man back safely.

sentences.zh: 自是知名，擢為正將，權發遣涇原路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: From then on he became renowned, was promoted to chief commander, and was made acting Director of Military Affairs for the Jingyuan Route.
translations.idiomatic: His fame dates from that day. He was promoted to chief commander and given acting charge of all Jingyuan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，涇原路經略使張中孚舉迪權知懷德軍，兼沿邊安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, Zhang Zhongfu, Military Commissioner of the Jingyuan Route, recommended Di as acting prefect of Huaide Army and concurrent Commissioner for Frontier Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: After the puppet Qi regime was set up, Zhang Zhongfu, commissioner of the Jingyuan Route, had Di appointed acting prefect of Huaide and frontier pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夏人合軍五萬薄懷德城，迪開門待之，夏人不敢入。

translations.literal: The Xia assembled fifty thousand troops and pressed against Huaide city; Di opened the gates to receive them, and the Xia did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia massed fifty thousand men against Huaide. Di threw open the gates as if inviting them in, and the Xia army did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 因以數千騎分門突出，遂破之，斬首五百級，獲軍資羊馬甚眾。

translations.literal: He then sent several thousand horsemen bursting out through separate gates, broke them, beheaded five hundred, and captured a great quantity of military stores, sheep, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent several thousand cavalry out through different gates, routed the enemy, took five hundred heads, and seized vast stores of supplies, sheep, and horses.

sentences.zh: 複破關師古兵，擢知涇州。

translations.literal: He again defeated the forces of Guan Shigu and was promoted to prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Guan Shigu's army as well and was promoted to prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未到官，改知鎮戎軍、沿邊安撫使。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he was transferred to prefect of Zhenrong Army and Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, he was reassigned as prefect of Zhenrong and frontier pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而權淮南東路馬步軍副總管，總制沂、密、淮陽，兼權知沂州。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made acting Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Huainan East Route Horse and Foot Forces, with overall control of Yi, Mi, and Huaiyang, and concurrent acting prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named acting deputy commander of Huainan East cavalry and infantry, with authority over Yi, Mi, and Huaiyang, and acting prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，去官。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he resigned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起複為環慶路兵馬都鈐轄，權知邠州。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to serve as Director of Military Affairs for the Huanqing Route and acting prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as director of Huanqing military affairs and acting prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，改華州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, he was made Defender of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi regime was abolished, he became defender of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，軍變，被執入山。

translations.literal: Before long a mutiny broke out, and he was seized and taken into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a mutiny erupted, and the rebels seized him and carried him into the hills.

sentences.zh: 已而賊眾悔曰：「公為政素善，豈宜劫辱。」

translations.literal: Before long the rebels regretted it and said, "Your governance has always been good—how can we hold you hostage and insult you?"
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers soon repented. "You have always governed us well," they said. "How can we hold you captive and dishonor you?"

sentences.zh: 遂縱之還，複領州事。

translations.literal: They then released him to return, and he resumed charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: So they let him go, and he resumed his duties as prefect.

sentences.zh: 海陵南伐，征斂煩急，官吏因緣為奸，富者用賄以免，貧者破產益困。

translations.literal: When Hailing marched south, levies were oppressively urgent; officials used the occasion for corruption; the wealthy bought exemption with bribes while the poor were ruined and driven deeper into hardship.
translations.idiomatic: During Hailing's southern campaign, requisitions grew crushing. Officials abused their power: the rich bought their way out with bribes, while the poor were ruined and driven still deeper into want.

sentences.zh: 迪悉召民使共議增減，不加威督而役力均，人情大悅。

translations.literal: Di summoned all the people to deliberate together on increases and reductions, applied no harsh coercion, and equalized labor obligations; popular sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Di called the people together to decide what levies to raise or cut. He imposed no harsh coercion, yet labor burdens were fairly shared, and the populace was deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙汾陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Fenyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Fenyang Army.

sentences.zh: 大定初，複為臨洮尹，遷南京路都轉運使，以省事惜費，安靜為政，河南稱之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, he again became Prefect of Lintao, was promoted to Chief Transport Commissioner of the Nanjing Route, and by simplifying administration and economizing expenses, governing quietly, won praise throughout Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era he again served as prefect of Lintao, then became chief transport commissioner on the Nanjing Route. He streamlined administration, cut waste, and governed without fuss; all Henan spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 徙絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年七十。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at seventy.

sentences.zh: 迪性純孝，父病，醫藥弗效，迪仰天泣禱，刲股作羹，由是獲安。

translations.literal: Di's nature was utterly filial; when his father fell ill and medicine proved ineffective, Di wept and prayed to Heaven, cut flesh from his thigh to make broth, and by this means his father recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Di was profoundly filial. When his father fell gravely ill and medicine failed, he wept and prayed heavenward, cut flesh from his own thigh to make a broth, and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 昆弟析家財，迪盡以與之，一無所取。

translations.literal: When his brothers divided the family property, Di gave them everything and took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his brothers divided the family estate, he gave them everything and kept nothing.

sentences.zh: 官爵之廕，率先諸侄。

translations.literal: When conferring hereditary privileges of office, he put his nephews ahead of his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever hereditary privileges of rank came due, he gave precedence to his nephews over his own children.

sentences.zh: 疾革，沐浴朝服而逝。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he bathed, donned court robes, and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, he bathed, dressed in his court robes, and died.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕移室懣

translations.literal: Wendihanyishimen
translations.idiomatic: Wendihanyishimen

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕移室懣，速頻屯懣歡春人，徙上京忽論失懶。

translations.literal: Wendihanyishimen was a man of Huanchun in Supintonmen; his family moved to Hulunshilan in Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihanyishimen came from Huanchun in the Supin district; his clan later moved to Hulunshilan in Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 兄朮輦，國初有功，授世襲謀克。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhunian had merit at the founding of the state and was granted a hereditary meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhunian had won distinction in the founding wars and received a hereditary meng'an commission.

sentences.zh: 移室懣性忠正強毅，善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Yishimen's nature was loyal, upright, and resolute; he was skilled in mounted archery, and his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Yishimen was loyal, upright, and unyielding, a fine horseman and archer whose raw strength surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，襲其兄謀克，積戰功，為洮州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, he inherited his brother's meng'an command, accumulated military achievements, and became Prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong he inherited his brother's meng'an post, won repeated honors in battle, and was made prefect of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「謀克，兄職也。

translations.literal: He said to others, "The meng'an command was my brother's office.
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "The meng'an belonged to my brother.

sentences.zh: 兄子斡魯古今已長矣。」

translations.literal: My brother's son Wolugu is already grown."
translations.idiomatic: His son Wolugu is grown now."

sentences.zh: 遂以謀克讓還兄子。

translations.literal: He therefore returned the meng'an command to his brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore restored the meng'an to his nephew.

sentences.zh: 宗弼聞而嘉之曰：「能讓世襲，可謂難矣。」

translations.literal: Zongbi heard of it and praised him, saying, "To yield a hereditary office—this is truly rare."
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi heard of it and commended him: "To surrender a hereditary commission—that is no small thing."

sentences.zh: 除貴德州刺史，改移典颭詳穩，遷烏古裏部族節度使，改德昌軍。

translations.literal: He was made Prefect of Guidezhou, transferred to Xiangwen of the Yidianfeng Office, promoted to Military Commissioner of the Wuguli Tribal Division, and then transferred to the Dechang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Guide, then xiangwen of the Yidianfeng office, then military commissioner of the Wuguli tribes, and finally commander of the Dechang Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年，大徵兵南伐，泰州猛安定遠阿補以所部叛還，移室懣以七謀克執定遠阿補，勒其眾付大軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenglong, during the great levy for the southern campaign, Andingyuan Abu of the Taizhou meng'an rebelled and returned with his command; Yishimen with seven meng'an commanders seized Andingyuan Abu and compelled his troops to submit to the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 4, during the mass mobilization for the southern war, Andingyuan Abu of the Taizhou meng'an rebelled and marched home. Yishimen took seven meng'an units, captured Abu, and handed his men over to the main force.

sentences.zh: 契丹反，敗會甯六猛安於締母嶺，屯于信、韓二州之境。

translations.literal: The Khitan rebelled, defeated the six meng'an of Huining at Dimuling, and encamped on the borders of Xin and Han prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan rose in revolt, they routed six Huining meng'an at Dimuling and camped along the frontiers of Xin and Han.

sentences.zh: 移室懣率數千人殺賊萬余于伊改河，以功遷臨潢尹。

translations.literal: Yishimen led several thousand men and killed more than ten thousand rebels at the Yigai River; for this merit he was promoted to Prefect of Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yishimen led several thousand men and killed more than ten thousand rebels on the Yigai River. For this feat he was made prefect of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，賜手詔曰：「南征諸路將士及卿子侄安遠、斡魯古、斜普兄弟，具甲仗悉來推戴，朕勉即大位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he bestowed a personal edict saying, "The generals and soldiers of the southern campaign routes, together with your sons and nephews Anyuan, Wolugu, and the Xiepu brothers, all came in full armor to urge my accession; I have reluctantly assumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne, he sent a personal edict: "The officers and men of the southern routes, together with your sons and nephews Anyuan, Wolugu, and the Xiepu brothers, all came in full armor to press the crown upon me. I have accepted the throne only with reluctance.

sentences.zh: 卿累世有功耆舊之臣，緣邊事未寧，臨潢劇任，姑仍舊職。

translations.literal: You are an elder minister of merit through successive generations; because frontier affairs are not yet settled and Linhuang is a weighty charge, for the present you remain in your former post.
translations.idiomatic: You are a veteran of many generations' service. Because the frontier is still unsettled and Linhuang is a post of the first importance, you are for now to keep your present office.

sentences.zh: 聞樞密副使白彥敬、南京留守紇石烈志寧來討契丹，今已遣人往招之。

translations.literal: I have heard that Vice Director of the Secretariat Bai Yanjing and Nanjing Military Governor Heshilie Zhining are coming to suppress the Khitan; I have now sent men to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Vice Director Bai Yanjing and Nanjing governor Heshilie Zhining are marching against the Khitan. I have already sent envoys to summon them.

sentences.zh: 其家皆在南京，恐或遁去，兼起異謀，若至則已，若不至，卿當以計執而獻之。

translations.literal: Their families are all in Nanjing; I fear they may flee, and at the same time hatch a separate plot. If they come, well and good; if they do not come, you should by stratagem seize them and present them to me.
translations.idiomatic: Their families are all in Nanjing, and I fear they may flee or hatch some other plot. If they come, so be it; if they do not, you must find a way to seize them and deliver them to me.

sentences.zh: 兩次遣人招誘招討都監老和尚，去人不知彼之所在，久而不還。

translations.literal: Twice I have sent men to summon and entice the Pacification Commissioner Laohéshang; the envoys did not know where he was, and long failed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Twice I have sent men to summon the pacification commissioner known as Old Monk; the envoys could not find him and were long overdue.

sentences.zh: 兼老和尚不知朕已即位，卿可使人諭以朕意。

translations.literal: Moreover, Old Monk does not know that I have already taken the throne; you may send someone to explain my intentions to him.
translations.idiomatic: Old Monk may not yet know that I have taken the throne. Send someone to make my intentions clear to him.

sentences.zh: 如來降，悉令復舊，邊關之事，可設耳目。」

translations.literal: If he comes to surrender, restore everything as before; on frontier affairs, you may set up informants."
translations.idiomatic: If he submits, restore all his former privileges. On frontier matters, establish whatever intelligence network you need."

sentences.zh: 是時窩斡已反，領兵數萬來攻臨潢，諸路軍未至，窩斡勢益大。

translations.literal: At this time Wowo had already rebelled, leading tens of thousands of troops to attack Linhuang; the armies of the various routes had not yet arrived, and Wowo's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wowo had already risen in revolt and was marching on Linhuang at the head of tens of thousands. Relief columns from other routes had not yet arrived, and Wowo's strength was growing daily.

sentences.zh: 移室懣領城中軍士六百人邀擊窩斡，凡數接戰，剿殺甚眾，所乘馬中流矢而僕，為賊所執。

translations.literal: Yishimen led six hundred soldiers of the city to intercept Wowo; after several engagements he killed a great many; the horse he rode was struck by a stray arrow and fell, and he was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yishimen led six hundred garrison troops out to intercept Wowo. After several sharp engagements he had killed a great many rebels, but his horse was struck by a stray arrow and fell, and the rebels seized him.

sentences.zh: 賊使移室懣招城中人曰：「爾生死在頃刻，能使城中出降，官爵如故；

translations.literal: The rebels made Yishimen summon the people of the city, saying, "Your lives and deaths hang in an instant; if you can make the city surrender, your offices and ranks will remain as before;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forced Yishimen to call to the city: "Your lives hang by a thread. If you surrender, your offices and ranks will stand as before;

sentences.zh: 不然殺汝矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise we will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise we will kill you all."

sentences.zh: 移室懣怒駡賊曰：「我受國家爵祿，肯從汝叛賊乎？」

translations.literal: Yishimen angrily cursed the rebels, saying, "I have received rank and stipend from the state—would I follow you rebel bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Yishimen cursed them in fury: "I have received rank and stipend from the state—do you think I would join you rebel dogs?"

sentences.zh: 賊執之至城中，迫脅之使招城中。

translations.literal: The rebels seized him and brought him to the city, coercing him to summon those within.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged him to the walls and tried to force him to call for surrender.

sentences.zh: 其妻子官屬將士皆登城臨望。

translations.literal: His wife, children, officials, and soldiers all climbed the walls to look down.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, children, officials, and soldiers climbed the battlements to watch.

sentences.zh: 移室懣厲聲曰：「我恨軍少不能滅賊。

translations.literal: Yishimen cried out in a stern voice, "I regret only that our troops were too few to destroy the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yishimen shouted in a voice that carried across the walls: "I regret only that our force was too small to destroy these rebels.

sentences.zh: 人生會有一死耳，汝輩慎勿降賊！

translations.literal: Every man's life must end in death—take care that none of you surrender to the rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Every man must die once—see that none of you surrenders to these bandits!

sentences.zh: 一旦開門納賊，城中百姓皆被殺掠，毋以我故敗國家事，賊無能為也。」

translations.literal: If you once open the gates and admit the rebels, all the common people in the city will be slaughtered and plundered. Do not for my sake ruin the affairs of the state and family—the rebels can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: If you open the gates to them, every soul in this city will be slaughtered and plundered. Do not ruin the state's cause on my account—these rebels cannot prevail."

sentences.zh: 賊怒殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels killed him in a rage.

sentences.zh: 城中人皆為之感激，推官麻珪益繕完城郭，右監軍神土懣、輔國上將軍阿思懣乘城固守。

translations.literal: All within the city were moved by him; the judicial officer Ma Gui further repaired and completed the walls and ramparts; the Right Military Supervisor Shen Tumen and the Assistant State-supporting General Asimen mounted the walls and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was deeply moved. Judicial officer Ma Gui redoubled the repairs to walls and towers; Right Military Supervisor Shen Tumen and Assistant State-supporting General Asimen manned the defenses and held fast.

sentences.zh: 賊不克攻，遂引眾東行。

translations.literal: The rebels could not take the city by assault and therefore led their forces eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to storm the city, the rebels marched east with their army.

sentences.zh: 神土懣

translations.literal: Shen Tumen
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tumen

sentences.zh: 神土懣，本諸宗室，贈銀青光祿大夫胡速魯改子也。

translations.literal: Shen Tumen was originally of the imperial clan, son of Husulugai, who had been posthumously awarded the Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tumen was of the imperial clan by birth, the son of Husulugai, who had been posthumously granted the rank of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 年十五，事太宗為左奉宸。

translations.literal: At the age of fifteen, he served Emperor Taizong as Left Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered service under Emperor Taizong as a left palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，充護衛，除武器署丞，累官肇州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, he served in the Guard Corps, was made Vice Director of the Weapons Office, and through successive promotions became Defender of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 he joined the Guard Corps, became vice director of the weapons office, and rose through successive posts to defender of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除元帥右都監，與咸平尹吾紮忽率泰州兵及曷懶路兵千五百人，會臨潢尹移室懣討契丹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, he was made Right Director of the Commander-in-Chief's Staff; together with Wuzhahu, Prefect of Xianping, he led the Taizhou troops and fifteen hundred men of the Yilan Route to join Linhuang Prefect Yishimen in suppressing the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he was appointed right director on the commander-in-chief's staff. With Xianping prefect Wuzhahu he led Taizhou troops and fifteen hundred men from the Yilan Route to join Linhuang prefect Yishimen against the Khitan rebels.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯臨潢，移室懣死，攻之不能克，乃引眾東行。

translations.literal: The Khitan attacked Linhuang; Yishimen died; they could not take the city by assault and therefore led their forces eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked Linhuang. Yishimen was killed in the fighting. Unable to take the city, the rebels marched east.

sentences.zh: 神土懣表乞濟師。

translations.literal: Shen Tumen submitted a memorial requesting reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tumen memorialized the throne asking for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲辰，世宗次海濱縣，得奏，上曰：「神土懣、吾紮忽軍不少，可以從長攻襲矣。」

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the twelfth month, Emperor Shizong halted at Haibin County; receiving the memorial, the emperor said, "The forces of Shen Tumen and Wuzhahu are not few—they can now carry out a sustained campaign of attack and harassment."
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the twelfth month, Shizong was encamped at Haibin County. When the memorial arrived, he said, "Shen Tumen and Wuzhahu have enough men now to pursue a sustained campaign of attack and harassment."

sentences.zh: 會右副元帥謀衍以大軍至，神土懣改曷速館節度使，隸右翼，與紇石烈志甯敗賊於長濼，戰霿𩃭河，皆有功，改婆速路兵馬都總管，卒。

translations.literal: When Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Mouyan arrived with the main army, Shen Tumen was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Yasuguan and attached to the right wing; together with Heshilie Zhining he defeated the rebels at Changpo and fought at the Menglu River, achieving merit in both; he was then made Chief Commander of Military Affairs for the Basu Route and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Deputy Commander Mouyan arrived with the main army, Shen Tumen was made military commissioner of Yasuguan and assigned to the right wing. With Heshilie Zhining he routed the rebels at Changpo and again at the Menglu River, winning distinction in both battles. He was then appointed chief commander of Basu military affairs and later died.

sentences.zh: 移剌成

translations.literal: Yila Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Yila Cheng

sentences.zh: 移剌成，本名落兀，其先遼橫帳人也。

translations.literal: Yila Cheng, original name Luowu, was by ancestry a man of the Liao Horizontal Account.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Cheng, whose original name was Luowu, came from the Liao imperial clan's Horizontal Account line.

sentences.zh: 沉勇有謀，通契丹、漢字。

translations.literal: Steadfast and brave, he possessed stratagems and was versed in Khitan and Chinese script.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and resourceful, he was literate in both Khitan and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 天會間，隸撻懶下為行軍猛安，與宋人戰于楚、泗之間，成以所部先登，大破宋軍，功最諸將。

translations.literal: During the Tianhui era, he was attached to Tawan as a campaign meng'an commander; fighting Song forces between Chu and Si, Cheng led his command in the first ascent, routed the Song army, and his merit surpassed all other generals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era he served under Tawan as a campaign meng'an commander. Fighting Song forces between Chu and Si, Cheng's unit was first over the wall, routed the Song army, and his merit outshone every other commander.

sentences.zh: 劉麟約會天長軍議進止。

translations.literal: Liu Lin arranged a meeting with the Tianchang army to discuss advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin arranged a conference with the Tianchang garrison to decide the next move.

sentences.zh: 成與夾古查合你俱為撻懶前鋒，得宋生口為鄉導，遂達天長，睿宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Cheng and Jiagu Zhaheni both served as Tawan's vanguard; they took a Song captive as guide and thus reached Tianchang; Prince Rui commended them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Jiagu Zhaheni both led Tawan's vanguard. They took a Song prisoner as guide and reached Tianchang; Prince Rui praised their achievement.

sentences.zh: 後從宗弼將兵廢齊國。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zongbi in leading troops to abolish the Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Zongbi in the campaign that abolished the Qi puppet regime.

sentences.zh: 及再伐宋，攻濠州，每戰輒先登，多所摧破。

translations.literal: When Song was attacked again, assaulting Haozhou, in every battle he was first to ascend and broke many enemy positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the second campaign against Song, assaulting Haozhou, he was first over the wall in battle after battle and broke enemy defenses wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再取河南，成及蕭懷忠等八猛安先渡。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again took Henan, Cheng and Xiao Huaizhong with eight meng'an commanders crossed the river first.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reconquered Henan, Cheng and Xiao Huaizhong led eight meng'an units across the river in the van.

sentences.zh: 河南平，第功授宣武將軍，除威州刺史。

translations.literal: When Henan was pacified, his merit was ranked and he was awarded the rank of Xuanwu General and made Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Henan was pacified, his merit was ranked and he received the rank of Xuanwu General and the prefecture of Wei.

sentences.zh: 用廉，擢同知延安尹，再遷昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Through a integrity review he was promoted to Vice Prefect of Yan'an and again transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Passed in an integrity review, he was promoted to vice prefect of Yan'an and later to military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆南伐，為武毅軍都總管。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong southern campaign, he was made Chief Commander of the Wuyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong southern campaign he served as chief commander of the Wuyi Army.

sentences.zh: 撒八反，海陵以事誅契丹名將，成以本軍守磁，即遣妻子還汴。

translations.literal: When Saba rebelled, Hailing executed famous Khitan generals on pretext; Cheng guarded Ci with his own army and immediately sent his wife and children back to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Saba rebelled, Hailing used the occasion to execute prominent Khitan generals. Cheng held Ci with his own troops and at once sent his family back to Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 海陵用是不疑。

translations.literal: Because of this Hailing did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing therefore never doubted his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時人高其有識。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his foresight.

sentences.zh: 改神武軍都總管，與孛朮魯定方為浙東道先鋒，使由淮陰進兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Commander of the Shenwu Army; together with Beipailu Dingfang he served as vanguard of the Zhedong Route, ordered to advance by way of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief commander of the Shenwu Army and, with Beipailu Dingfang, led the Zhedong vanguard advancing from Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 以所部護糧赴揚州，敵兵乘夜來攻，成整兵奮擊，斬刈甚眾。

translations.literal: Leading his command to escort grain to Yangzhou, enemy troops attacked by night; Cheng arrayed his forces and struck fiercely, killing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting grain to Yangzhou with his troops, he was attacked at night by the enemy. Cheng formed his men and counterattacked fiercely, killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 會海陵庶人死，軍還，複鎮昭義。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Prince Hailing died, the army returned, and he again garrisoned Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed Emperor Hailing died, the army withdrew, and Cheng again took command at Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，以廉在優等，改河中尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, through an integrity review he ranked in the superior grade and was made Prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he ranked in the top grade on an integrity review and was appointed prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 再除臨洮尹，招降喬家等族首領結什角。

translations.literal: He was again made Prefect of Lintao and induced the surrender of Jieshijiao, leader of the Qiao clan and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed prefect of Lintao and won the submission of Jieshijiao, chief of the Qiao clan and allied tribes.

sentences.zh: 遷南京留守，召拜樞密副使，封任國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Military Governor of Nanjing, summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing military governor, was summoned to court as vice director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Renguo.

sentences.zh: 改北京留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military governor of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上悼惜之，授其子順思阿不武功將軍，世襲咸平路鈔赤鄰猛安下查不魯謀克。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor mourned him with regret, awarded his son Shunsiabu the rank of Wugong General, and granted hereditary succession to the Chabulu meng'an command under the Chaochilin meng'an of the Xianping Route.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death reached the throne, the emperor mourned him with deep regret. His son Shunsiabu received the rank of Wugong General and inherited the Chabulu meng'an post under the Chaochilin meng'an on the Xianping Route.

sentences.zh: 結什角者，西番既衰，其苗裔曰堇氈，其子曰巴氈。

translations.literal: As for Jieshijiao: after the Western Tribes declined, their descendant was called Jinzhan, and his son was called Bazhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshijiao came from the western tribes. After their power waned, one line descended through Jinzhan to his son Bazhan.

sentences.zh: 角始附宋，賜姓趙，改名順忠。

translations.literal: Jijiao at first submitted to Song, was granted the surname Zhao, and renamed Shunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshijiao first submitted to Song, was granted the surname Zhao, and took the name Shunzhong.

sentences.zh: 順忠子永吉，永吉子世昌，皆受宋官，為左武大夫，遙領萊州防禦使，襲把羊族長。

translations.literal: Shunzhong's son Yongji and Yongji's son Shichang all received Song offices, served as Left Martial Grand Master, held the distant post of Defender of Laizhou, and inherited leadership of the Bayang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhong's son Yongji and Yongji's son Shichang all held Song offices as Left Martial Grand Master and nominal defender of Laizhou, and inherited leadership of the Bayang clan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷定陝西，世昌換忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: When the court pacified Shaanxi, Shichang was transferred to the rank of Zhongyi Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: After the court secured Shaanxi, Shichang was given the Jin rank of Zhongyi Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 既而鬼蘆族長京臧殺世昌，朝廷遣兵執京臧，斬之臨洮市，以世昌子鐵哥為把羊族都管。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzang, leader of the Guilu clan, killed Shichang; the court sent troops to seize Jingzang and executed him in the market at Lintao, making Shichang's son Tiege overall chief of the Bayang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Jingzang, chief of the Guilu clan, killed Shichang. The court sent troops to seize Jingzang and executed him in the Lintao marketplace, appointing Shichang's son Tiege as overall chief of the Bayang clan.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，宋人破洮州，鐵哥弟結什角與其母走入喬家族避之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, Song forces took Taozhou; Tiege's younger brother Jieshijiao and his mother fled into the Qiao clan territory to escape.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4, when Song forces captured Taozhou, Tiege's younger brother Jieshijiao and his mother fled for refuge among the Qiao clan.

sentences.zh: 喬家族首領播逋與鄰族木波隴逋、龐拜、丙離四族耆老大僧等立結什角為木波四族長，號曰「王子」。

translations.literal: Bobo, leader of the Qiao clan, together with the neighboring tribes of Mubo, Longbo, Pangbai, and Bingli and their elders including Daseng, installed Jieshijiao as chief of the four Mubo tribes and styled him "Prince."
translations.idiomatic: Bobo, chief of the Qiao clan, together with the neighboring Mubo, Longbo, Pangbai, and Bingli tribes and their elders, including Daseng, installed Jieshijiao as chief of the four Mubo tribes and hailed him as "Prince."

sentences.zh: 其地北接洮州、積石軍。

translations.literal: Their territory on the north bordered Taozhou and Jishi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands bordered Taozhou and the Jishi garrison to the north.

sentences.zh: 其南隴逋族，南限大山，八百餘裏不通人行。

translations.literal: To their south was the Longbo tribe; southward great mountains barred the way, and for more than eight hundred li no human passage was possible.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay the Longbo tribe, beyond which great mountains stretched for more than eight hundred li without a passable trail.

sentences.zh: 東南與疊州羌接。

translations.literal: Southeast they bordered the Qiang of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast they bordered the Qiang of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 其西丙離族，西與盧甘羌接。

translations.literal: To their west was the Bingli tribe; westward they bordered the Qiang of Lugan.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay the Bingli tribe, beyond which lived the Qiang of Lugan.

sentences.zh: 其北龐拜族，與西夏容魯族接。

translations.literal: To their north was the Pangbai tribe, bordering the Ronglu clan of Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay the Pangbai tribe, bordering the Ronglu clan of Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 地高寒，無絲枲五穀，惟產青稞，與野菜合酥酪食之。

translations.literal: The land was high and cold; there were no silk, hemp, or the five grains—only highland barley was produced, which together with wild vegetables and butter curds served as food.
translations.idiomatic: The country was high and cold, without silk, hemp, or the five grains. Only barley grew there, eaten with wild greens and curds.

sentences.zh: 其疆境共八千里，合四萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Their territory in all extended eight thousand li, comprising more than forty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory stretched eight thousand li in all, with more than forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其居隨水草畜牧，遷徙不常。

translations.literal: Their dwellings followed water and pasture for herding; they migrated without fixed abode.
translations.idiomatic: They followed pasture and water with their herds and had no fixed settlements.

sentences.zh: 結什角念朝廷為其父報仇，欲棄四族歸朝，四族不許。

translations.literal: Jieshijiao, mindful that the court had avenged his father, wished to abandon the four tribes and submit to the dynasty, but the four tribes would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful that the court had avenged his father, Jieshijiao wished to leave the four tribes and submit to the Jin, but they would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 成至臨洮，使人招結什角，乃率四族來附，進馬百匹，仍請每年貢馬。

translations.literal: When Cheng arrived at Lintao, he sent men to summon Jieshijiao; Jieshijiao then led the four tribes to submit, presented one hundred horses, and requested to present horses annually as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng reached Lintao, he sent envoys to summon Jieshijiao, who then led the four tribes to submit. He presented one hundred horses and asked to send horses in tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「遠人慕義，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Distant peoples admire righteousness—We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "These distant peoples have come in admiration of our righteousness, and We are deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 其遣能吏往撫其眾，厚其賞賜。」

translations.literal: Dispatch capable officials to pacify their people and bestow generous rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Send able officials to win over their people and grant them generous rewards."

sentences.zh: 初，天會中，詔以舊積石地與夏人，夏人謂之祈安城。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Tianhui, an edict ceded the old Jishi territory to the Xia; the Xia called it Qi'an City.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tianhui era, an edict had ceded the old Jishi territory to Western Xia, which called it Qi'an City.

sentences.zh: 有莊浪四族，一曰吹折門，二曰密臧門，三曰隴逋門，四曰龐拜門，雖屬夏國，叛服不常。

translations.literal: There were the four Zhuanglang tribes: first, the Chuizhemen; second, the Mizangmen; third, the Longbomen; fourth, the Pangbaimen. Though subject to Xia, their submission and rebellion were inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: Four Zhuanglang tribes—the Chuizhemen, Mizangmen, Longbomen, and Pangbaimen—were nominally subject to Xia but shifted between rebellion and submission.

sentences.zh: 大定六年，夏人破滅吹折、密臧二門，其隴逋、龐拜二門與喬家族相鄰，遂歸結什角。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading, the Xia destroyed the Chuizhe and Mizang gates; the Longbo and Pangbai gates, neighboring the Qiao clan, thereupon submitted to Jieshijiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 6 the Xia destroyed the Chuizhe and Mizang gates. The Longbo and Pangbai gates, neighboring the Qiao clan, then joined Jieshijiao.

sentences.zh: 夏國遣使來告莊浪族違命作亂，欲興兵剪除。

translations.literal: The Xia state sent envoys to report that the Zhuanglang tribes had defied orders and risen in rebellion, and that they wished to raise troops to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia sent envoys reporting that the Zhuanglang tribes had rebelled and asking permission to march against them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知隴逋、龐拜二門舊屬夏國，報以將檢會其地舊所隸屬，毋擅出兵。

translations.literal: The court did not know that the Longbo and Pangbai gates had formerly belonged to Xia, and replied that it would investigate to which jurisdiction the territory had originally belonged and that they must not send troops on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The court, unaware that the Longbo and Pangbai gates had once belonged to Xia, replied that it would investigate the territory's former jurisdiction and forbade Xia to send troops on its own.

sentences.zh: 結什角之母居於莊浪族中。

translations.literal: Jieshijiao's mother dwelt among the Zhuanglang tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshijiao's mother lived among the Zhuanglang tribes.

sentences.zh: 大定九年，結什角往省其母，夏人伺知之，遂出兵圍結什角，招之使降。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dading, Jieshijiao went to visit his mother; the Xia learned of it and sent troops to surround Jieshijiao, summoning him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 9, when Jieshijiao went to visit his mother, the Xia learned of it, surrounded him with troops, and urged him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 結什角不從，率所部力戰，潰圍出，夏人斫斷其臂，虜其母去，部兵亦多亡者。

translations.literal: Jieshijiao refused; leading his command he fought fiercely, broke through the encirclement, but the Xia hacked off his arm and carried off his mother; many of his troops also perished.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and fought his way out at the head of his men, but the Xia severed his arm, seized his mother, and killed many of his followers.

sentences.zh: 結什角尋亦死，遺言請命朝廷，複立喬家族首領。

translations.literal: Jieshijiao soon died as well, leaving a request that the court be petitioned to reestablish a leader of the Qiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshijiao soon died as well, leaving word that the court should be asked to install a new Qiao clan chief.

sentences.zh: 陝西奏：「聞知夏國王李仁孝與其臣任得敬中分其國，發兵四萬，役夫三萬，築祈安城，殺喬家等族首領結什角。

translations.literal: Shaanxi memorialized: "We have learned that the Xia king Li Renxiao and his minister Ren Dede are dividing the state between them, have raised forty thousand troops and thirty thousand laborers, built Qi'an City, and killed Jieshijiao, leader of the Qiao clan and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi reported: "We hear that the Xia king Li Renxiao and his minister Ren Dede are splitting the realm between them. They have raised forty thousand troops and thirty thousand laborers, built Qi'an City, and killed Jieshijiao, chief of the Qiao clan and allied tribes.

sentences.zh: 屢獲宋諜人，言宋欲結夏國謀犯邊境。」

translations.literal: Song spies have repeatedly been captured, saying that Song wishes to ally with Xia to plot an invasion of the border."
translations.idiomatic: We have repeatedly captured Song spies who say Song seeks an alliance with Xia to raid our border."

sentences.zh: 詔遣大理卿李昌圖、左司員外郎粘割斡特剌往按之，且止夏人毋築祈安城及處置喬家等族別立首領。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Grand Justice Li Changtu and Left Department Vice Director Nian'ge Wate to investigate, and also ordered the Xia to cease building Qi'an City and to deal with the Qiao clan and other tribes by separately installing leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Grand Justice Li Changtu and Left Department Vice Director Nian'ge Wate to investigate, and ordered Xia to stop building Qi'an City and to install separate chiefs for the Qiao clan and allied tribes.

sentences.zh: 夏國報雲：「祈安本積石舊城，久廢，邊臣請設戍兵鎮撫莊浪族，所以備盜，非有他也。

translations.literal: The Xia state replied: "Qi'an was originally the old Jishi city, long abandoned; frontier officials requested garrison troops to pacify the Zhuanglang tribes—this was solely to guard against bandits, with no other purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Xia replied: "Qi'an is the old Jishi fortress, long abandoned. Our frontier officials asked for a garrison to pacify the Zhuanglang tribes—nothing more than bandit control.

sentences.zh: 結什角以兵入境，以是殺之，不知為喬家族首領也。」

translations.literal: Jieshijiao entered our territory with troops; for this reason he was killed—we did not know he was leader of the Qiao clan."
translations.idiomatic: Jieshijiao crossed our border with armed men, so we killed him. We did not know he was chief of the Qiao clan."

sentences.zh: 李昌圖等按視，殺結什角之地本在夏境，築祈安城已畢工，皆罷歸，不得宋、夏交通之狀，乃于熙秦迫近宋、夏沖要量添戍兵。

translations.literal: Li Changtu and others investigated on the spot: the place where Jieshijiao was killed lay within Xia territory, and construction of Qi'an City was already complete; all withdrew without finding evidence of Song-Xia collusion; they then added garrison troops at key points in Xi-Qin near the Song-Xia frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changtu's mission found that Jieshijiao had been killed inside Xia territory and that Qi'an City was already finished. They returned without proof of a Song-Xia plot and recommended additional garrisons at strategic points in the Xi-Qin region along the Song-Xia frontier.

sentences.zh: 及問喬家等族民戶，願以結什角侄趙師古為首領，於是詔以趙師古為木波喬家、丙離、隴逋、龐拜四族都鈐轄，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: When the households of the Qiao clan and other tribes were questioned, they wished Jieshijiao's nephew Zhao Shigu to be leader; an edict thereupon made Zhao Shigu overall director of the four tribes of Mubo, Qiao, Bingli, Longbo, and Pangbai, with the added rank of Xuanwu General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiao and allied clans were consulted, they asked for Jieshijiao's nephew Zhao Shigu as chief. The throne appointed Zhao Shigu overall director of the Mubo, Qiao, Bingli, Longbo, and Pangbai tribes and gave him the rank of Xuanwu General.

sentences.zh: 石抹卞

translations.literal: Shi Mobian
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mobian

sentences.zh: 石抹卞，本名阿魯古列。

translations.literal: Shi Mobian, original name Alugulie.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mobian, whose original name was Alugulie.

sentences.zh: 五代祖王五，遼駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Wang Wu was Commandant of the Liao Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Wang Wu had been commandant of the Liao imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 父五斤，為群牧使，從睿宗秋山，卞年十三，已能射，連獲二鹿，睿宗奇之，賜以良馬及金吐鶻。

translations.literal: His father Wujin served as Commissioner of Herds; following Prince Rui on the autumn hunt, Bian at thirteen could already shoot and in succession took two deer; Prince Rui marveled at this and bestowed on him a fine horse and a gold gyrfalcon.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wujin was commissioner of herds. On a hunt with Prince Rui, the thirteen-year-old Bian brought down two deer in succession. The prince was astonished and gave him a fine horse and a gold gyrfalcon.

sentences.zh: 天會末，宗弼為右監軍，召卞隸帳下。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianhui, Zongbi was Right Military Supervisor and summoned Bian to serve under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianhui era, Zongbi, then right military supervisor, took Bian into his staff.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，是時宗磐為太師，撻懶為左副元帥，人爭附之，使人召卞，卞不往。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning; at that time Zongpan was Grand Preceptor and Tawan was Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief; people vied to attach themselves to them and sent men to summon Bian, but Bian did not go.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father, he was summoned by Zongpan the Grand Preceptor and Tawan the left deputy commander, to whom many were flocking—but Bian refused to go.

sentences.zh: 宗磐、撻懶皆以罪誅，人多其有識。

translations.literal: Zongpan and Tawan were both executed for their crimes, and many people admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were later executed for treason, and many admired Bian's judgment.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複取河南，與宋人戰於潁州，漢軍少卻，卞身被七創，率勇士十余騎奮擊，敗之。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again took Henan and fought Song forces at Yingzhou, the Han army briefly gave ground; Bian suffered seven wounds, led more than ten brave horsemen in a fierce charge, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reconquered Henan and fought Song at Yingzhou, the Han contingent wavered. Bian took seven wounds, led a dozen horsemen in a desperate charge, and turned the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 及宋稱臣，宗弼選嘗有勞者與俱入朝，授卞忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: When Song submitted as a vassal, Zongbi selected those who had rendered merit to enter court with him and awarded Bian the rank of Zhongyong Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: When Song submitted, Zongbi took his most deserving officers to court and gave Bian the rank of Zhongyong Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 遷宣武將軍，除河間少尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Xuanwu General and made Vice Prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Xuanwu General and made vice prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 察廉，升遂州刺史，改壽州，再改唐州。

translations.literal: Through an integrity review he was promoted to Prefect of Suizhou, transferred to Shouzhou, and again to Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Passed in an integrity review, he rose to prefect of Suizhou, then Shouzhou, and finally Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去官，起複唐州刺史。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office; he was recalled to serve again as Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother, then was recalled as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，卞為武毅軍都總管，由別道進兵。

translations.literal: When Hailing attacked Song, Bian was Chief Commander of the Wuyi Army and advanced by a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: During Hailing's campaign against Song, Bian served as chief commander of the Wuyi Army on a separate line of advance.

sentences.zh: 遇宋伏兵數百人，以三十騎擊敗之，遂下信陽軍及羅山縣。

translations.literal: He encountered several hundred Song ambush troops and with thirty horsemen defeated them, then took Xinyang Army and Luoshan County.
translations.idiomatic: He met several hundred Song ambushers and routed them with thirty horsemen, then captured Xinyang and Luoshan.

sentences.zh: 至蔣州，宋守將棄城遁，因取其城。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangzhou, the Song defender abandoned the city and fled; he thereupon took the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou the Song commander fled, and Bian took the city without a fight.

sentences.zh: 頃之，軍士皆欲逃歸，闌子山猛安結漢軍三猛安謀克劫卞還，舍于獎水之曲。

translations.literal: Before long the soldiers all wished to flee home; the Lanshan meng'an commander, together with three Han meng'an commanders, plotted to seize Bian and return, detaining him on the bend of the Jiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his men wanted to desert homeward. The Lanshan meng'an commander and three Han meng'an officers plotted to seize Bian and march back, holding him on a bend of the Jiang River.

sentences.zh: 卞乃陰約漢軍將吏乘夜掩殺闌子山猛安，複將其軍。

translations.literal: Bian secretly arranged with the Han officers and clerks to strike by night and kill the Lanshan meng'an commander, then again took command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bian secretly won the Han officers to his side and by night killed the Lanshan commander, then resumed command of the army.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，除鄭州防禦使，以本官領行軍萬戶伐宋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, he was made Defender of Zhengzhou and, retaining that office, led a campaign wanhu in attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he became defender of Zhengzhou and led a campaign wanhu against Song in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 遷武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 宋人請和，明年，有水牛數百頭自淮南走入州境，僚佐欲收之充官用，卞不聽，複驅過淮還之。

translations.literal: Song sought peace; the next year several hundred water buffalo strayed from Huainan into the prefecture; subordinates wished to seize them for official use, but Bian would not permit it and drove them back across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: After Song sued for peace, several hundred water buffalo wandered from Huainan into his jurisdiction the next year. His staff wanted to seize them for the government, but Bian refused and drove them back across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹，轉西南路招討使，改大名尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Prefect of Henan, transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route, and made Prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Henan, then pacification commissioner on the Southwest Route, then prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 大名多盜，而城郭不完，卞請修大名城。

translations.literal: Daming had many bandits, yet its walls and moats were incomplete; Bian requested repairs to the walls of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Daming was rife with bandits, yet its walls were in ruins. Bian petitioned to rebuild them.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 城完葺，盜賊不得發。

translations.literal: When the walls were fully repaired, bandits could no longer rise.
translations.idiomatic: Once the walls were complete, banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 徙臨洮尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 楊仲武

translations.literal: Yang Zhongwu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongwu

sentences.zh: 楊仲武，字德威，保安人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhongwu, style name Dewei, was a man of Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongwu, whose style was Dewei, came from Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 父遇，以勇聞關西，為宥州團練使。

translations.literal: His father Yu was famed for valor in the western passes and served as Regiment Trainer of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was famed for courage in the western passes and served as regiment trainer of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋末，仲武謁經略使王庶求自效，遂用為先鋒。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, Zhongwu visited Military Commissioner Wang Shu to offer his service and was employed as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song era he sought out Military Commissioner Wang Shu and was made a vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 婁室入關，仲武與鄜延路兵馬都監鄭建充俱降，為安塞堡。

translations.literal: When Wushil entered the pass, Zhongwu and Zheng Jianchong, Director of Military Affairs for the Yan'an Route, both surrendered and was made commander of An Sai Fort,
translations.idiomatic: When Wushil entered the pass, Zhongwu and Zheng Jianchong, director of Yan'an military affairs, both surrendered and were appointed commander of An Sai Fort

sentences.zh: 環慶路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Director of Military Affairs for the Huanqing Route.
translations.idiomatic: and director of military affairs on the Huanqing Route.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，複陝西，將兵戍鳳翔，屢卻宋軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, Shaanxi was recovered; he led troops to garrison Fengxiang and repeatedly repelled Song forces.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong, when Shaanxi was recovered, he garrisoned Fengxiang and repeatedly drove back Song attacks.

sentences.zh: 除知寧州。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 關中薦饑，境內盜賊縱橫，仲武悉平之。

translations.literal: Famine spread through Guanzhong; bandits ran rampant within his jurisdiction, and Zhongwu pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Guanzhong and bandits overran his territory, Zhongwu suppressed them all.

sentences.zh: 改坊州刺史，複知寧州，遷同知臨洮尹，改同知河中府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Fangzhou, again made Administrator of Ningzhou, promoted to Vice Prefect of Lintao, and transferred to Vice Prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Fangzhou, again as administrator of Ningzhou, then as vice prefect of Lintao and vice prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 海陵營繕南京，典浮橋工役。

translations.literal: When Hailing undertook construction at Nanjing, he oversaw the pontoon-bridge works.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing rebuilt Nanjing, he supervised work on the pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 臨洮地接西羌，與木波雜居，邊將貪暴，木波苦之，遂相率為寇掠。

translations.literal: Lintao bordered the western Qiang and was intermixed with the Mubo; frontier generals were greedy and brutal; the Mubo suffered under them and therefore banded together in raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Lintao bordered the western Qiang and was intermixed with the Mubo tribes. Greedy frontier officers oppressed them until the Mubo rose together in raids.

sentences.zh: 仲武前治臨洮，乃從數騎入其營諭之曰：「此皆將校侵漁汝等，以至此爾。

translations.literal: Zhongwu had formerly governed Lintao; he then went with only a few horsemen into their camp and instructed them, saying, "All this is because officers and commanders have preyed upon you, bringing you to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu, who had governed Lintao before, rode into their camp with only a few men and told them: "Your troubles come from officers who have preyed on you.

sentences.zh: 今懲治此輩，不復擾害汝也。」

translations.literal: Now these men will be punished, and you will no longer be harassed."
translations.idiomatic: They will be punished now, and you will be left in peace."

sentences.zh: 並以禍福曉之。

translations.literal: He also explained to them the consequences of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained what reward or ruin would follow their choices.

sentences.zh: 羌人喜悅，寇掠遂息。

translations.literal: The Qiang were delighted, and raiding ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were pleased, and the raids stopped.

sentences.zh: 至是，木波複掠熙河，熙河主帥使人諭之，不肯去，曰：「楊總管來，我乃解去。」

translations.literal: At this time the Mubo again raided Xihe; the Xihe commander sent men to instruct them, but they would not withdraw, saying, "Only when Commissioner Yang comes will we disperse."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Mubo raided Xihe again. The Xihe commander sent envoys, but they would not withdraw, saying, "We will leave only when Commissioner Yang comes."

sentences.zh: 熙河具奏，詔複遣仲武。

translations.literal: Xihe submitted a full report, and an edict again dispatched Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xihe reported this to court, and an edict sent Zhongwu back.

sentences.zh: 當是時，木波謂仲武不能複來。

translations.literal: At that time the Mubo believed Zhongwu could not come again.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Mubo assumed he would not return.

sentences.zh: 及仲武至，與其酋帥相見，責以負約，對曰：「邊將苦我，今之來，求訴于上官耳。

translations.literal: When Zhongwu arrived and met their chieftains, he reproached them for breaking their pledge; they replied, "Frontier generals have tormented us; our coming now is only to appeal to our superiors.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwu arrived and met their chiefs, he rebuked them for breaking faith. They answered: "Frontier officers have tormented us. We have come only to appeal to our superiors.

sentences.zh: 今幸見公，願終身不復犯塞。」

translations.literal: Now, fortunate to see you, we wish never again to violate the border."
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have met you, we swear never again to raid the frontier."

sentences.zh: 乃舉酒酹天，折箭為誓。

translations.literal: They then raised wine to libate Heaven and broke arrows in oath.
translations.idiomatic: They poured wine to Heaven and broke arrows in oath.

sentences.zh: 仲武因以卮酒飲之曰：「當更為汝請，若複背約，必用兵矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongwu thereupon drank with them from a cup and said, "I shall again plead your case for you; if you again break your pledge, troops will certainly be used."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu drank with them and said: "I will plead your case again. But if you break faith once more, the army will come."

sentences.zh: 羌人羅拜而去。

translations.literal: The Qiang bowed in ranks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes bowed in ranks and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，以仲武為威定軍都總管，駐兵歸德。

translations.literal: When Song was attacked, Zhongwu was made Chief Commander of the Weiding Army and stationed troops at Guide.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Song he was made chief commander of the Weiding Army and encamped at Guide.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，除武勝軍節度使，改陝西西路轉運使，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading, he was made Military Commissioner of the Wusheng Army, transferred to Transport Commissioner of the Shaanxi West Route, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 he became military commissioner of the Wusheng Army, then transport commissioner on the Shaanxi West Route, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 蒲察世傑

translations.literal: Pucha Shijie
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Shijie

sentences.zh: 蒲察世傑，本名阿撒，曷速館斡篤河人，徙遼陽。

translations.literal: Pucha Shijie, original name Asa, was a man of Wuduh River in Yasuguan; his family moved to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Shijie, whose original name was Asa, came from Wuduh River in Yasuguan; his family later moved to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 初在梁王宗弼軍中。

translations.literal: He first served in the army of Prince Liang, Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in Prince Liang Zongbi's army.

sentences.zh: 為人多力，每與武士角力賭羊，輒勝之。

translations.literal: He was a man of great strength; whenever he wrestled with warriors wagering sheep, he invariably won.
translations.idiomatic: A man of exceptional strength, he invariably won whenever he wrestled other warriors for wagers of sheep.

sentences.zh: 能以拳擊四歲牛，折脅死之。

translations.literal: He could strike a four-year-old ox with his fists, break its ribs, and kill it.
translations.idiomatic: He could kill a four-year-old ox with his bare fists, breaking its ribs in the process.

sentences.zh: 有糧車陷淖中，七牛挽不能出，世傑手挽出之。

translations.literal: Once a grain cart sank into mud; seven oxen pulling could not extract it, but Shijie pulled it out by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once a grain cart sank into the mud. Seven oxen could not pull it free, but Shijie hauled it out with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 宗敏為東京留守，召置左右。

translations.literal: When Zongmin served as Eastern Capital military governor, he summoned Shijie and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin was military governor of the Eastern Capital, he summoned Shijie and kept him in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，即以為護衛。

translations.literal: When Hailing seized the throne, Shijie was immediately made an imperial guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing usurped the throne, Shijie was at once appointed to the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂世傑曰：「汝勇力絕倫，今我兄弟有異志者，期以十日除之，則有非常之賞，仍盡以各人家產賜汝。」

translations.literal: Hailing said to Shijie: "Your courage and strength are peerless. If any of my brothers now harbors disloyal intent, eliminate him within ten days, and you shall receive an extraordinary reward; I shall furthermore bestow upon you the entire household property of each man."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told Shijie: "Your courage and strength are unmatched. If any of my brothers now plots against me, kill him within ten days and I will give you an extraordinary reward — and I will bestow on you each man's entire estate besides."

sentences.zh: 世傑受詔而不肯為。

translations.literal: Shijie received the edict but refused to act.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie accepted the order but refused to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 已過十日，海陵怒，面責之。

translations.literal: After the ten days had passed, Hailing was enraged and berated him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: When the ten days were up, Hailing flew into a rage and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 世傑曰：「臣自誓不以非道害物，雖死不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Shijie said: "Your servant has sworn never to harm others by wrongful means; though I die, I dare not obey this edict."
translations.idiomatic: Shijie said: "I have sworn never to harm anyone by unjust means. Even if it costs me my life, I dare not obey this order."

sentences.zh: 海陵愛其勇，不之罪也。

translations.literal: Hailing admired his courage and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing admired his courage and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年，調諸路兵伐宋，年二十以上、五十以下皆籍之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenglong, troops from the various routes were mobilized to attack Song; all men from twenty years and above to fifty and below were registered.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 4 troops were levied from every circuit for the campaign against Song, and all men between twenty and fifty were registered for service.

sentences.zh: 他使者唯恐不如詔書，得數多，世傑往喝懶路，得數少。

translations.literal: Other envoys, fearing they might fall short of the edict, registered large numbers; when Shijie went to the Yilan Route, he registered fewer.
translations.idiomatic: The other envoys, afraid of falling short of the quota set by the edict, registered as many men as they could. Shijie, sent to the Yilan Route, registered far fewer.

sentences.zh: 海陵怪問之，對曰：「曷懶地接高麗，今若多籍其丁，即有緩急，何以為備？」

translations.literal: Hailing questioned this in surprise; Shijie replied: "The Yilan region borders Goryeo. If we now register many of its able-bodied men, when emergency arises, with what shall we defend ourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing questioned him in surprise. Shijie answered: "The Yilan region borders Goryeo. If we register too many of its men now, what will we have left for defense when trouble comes?"

sentences.zh: 海陵喜曰：「他人用心不能及也。」

translations.literal: Hailing said with pleasure: "Others cannot match your forethought."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said with approval: "No one else thinks as far ahead as you do."

sentences.zh: 除同知安國軍節度使事，賜銀二百五十兩、絹彩六百匹、馬二疋。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Anguo Army, and given two hundred fifty taels of silver, six hundred bolts of silk, and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the Anguo Army and rewarded with two hundred fifty taels of silver, six hundred bolts of silk, and two horses.

sentences.zh: 是時徵發不已，民不堪命，犯法者眾，邢久無長吏，獄囚積四百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time levies never ceased, the people could not endure their burdens, lawbreakers were many, Xing Prefecture long lacked a chief official, and more than four hundred prisoners accumulated in the jails.
translations.idiomatic: Levies in those days never let up. The people were crushed under their burdens, crime was widespread, Xing Prefecture had gone long without a chief magistrate, and more than four hundred prisoners had piled up in the jails.

sentences.zh: 世傑到官月餘，決遣略盡。

translations.literal: Within a month and more after Shijie took office, he adjudicated and released nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of taking office, Shijie had tried and cleared nearly the entire backlog.

sentences.zh: 入為宿直將軍，以事往胡裏改路，還奏：「契丹部族大抵皆叛，百姓驚擾不安。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Palace Duty General. On a mission to the Huligai Route, he returned and reported: "The Khitan tribes have for the most part all rebelled; the common people are alarmed and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as a palace duty general. Sent on business to the Huligai Route, he returned and reported: "The Khitan tribes have largely risen in revolt, and the people are terrified and unsettled.

sentences.zh: 今舉國南伐，賊若乘虛入據東土根本之地，雖得江、淮，無益也。

translations.literal: Now with the entire state marching south, if the rebels seize the opportunity to enter and occupy the fundamental lands of the eastern territories, even if we gain the Yangtze and Huai, it will be of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If the whole realm marches south now and the rebels seize the chance to occupy the heartland of the east, gaining the Yangtze and Huai will do us no good.

sentences.zh: 宜先討平契丹，南伐未晚。」

translations.literal: We should first pacify the Khitan; it is not too late to attack south afterward."
translations.idiomatic: We should put down the Khitan first. The southern campaign can wait."

sentences.zh: 海陵不悅曰：「詔令已出矣。

translations.literal: Hailing, displeased, said: "The edict has already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, displeased, said: "The orders have already gone out.

sentences.zh: 今以三萬兵選將屯中都以北，足以鎮壓。」

translations.literal: Send thirty thousand troops under selected generals to garrison north of the Central Capital — that will be sufficient to suppress them."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand picked troops stationed north of the Central Capital under chosen generals will be enough to hold them down."

sentences.zh: 世傑又曰：「若東土大族附於賊，恐三萬眾未易當也。」

translations.literal: Shijie said again: "If the great clans of the eastern territories attach themselves to the rebels, I fear thirty thousand men will not easily suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Shijie pressed on: "If the great clans of the east join the rebels, I doubt thirty thousand men will be enough."

sentences.zh: 海陵不聽。

translations.literal: Hailing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 及發汴京，授鄭州防禦使，領武捷軍副總管。

translations.literal: When the army departed from Bianjing, Shijie was appointed defender of Zheng Prefecture and made deputy chief commander of the Wujie Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army set out from Bianjing, he was made defender of Zheng Prefecture and deputy chief commander of the Wujie Army.

sentences.zh: 大軍渡淮，世傑以軍三千護糧餫東下，敗宋兵數千人，奪其戰船甚眾。

translations.literal: When the main army crossed the Huai, Shijie with three thousand men escorted grain supplies downstream, defeated several thousand Song troops, and captured a great many of their warships.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army crossed the Huai, Shijie led three thousand men escorting grain supplies downstream. He routed several thousand Song troops and captured a large number of their warships.

sentences.zh: 至和州境，擊宋兵五萬人走之。

translations.literal: Reaching the border of He Prefecture, he attacked fifty thousand Song troops and put them to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the border of He Prefecture, he attacked a Song force of fifty thousand and put it to flight.

sentences.zh: 明日，使其子兀迭領二百八十騎為應兵，自領八百騎前戰。

translations.literal: The next day he had his son Wudie lead two hundred eighty horsemen as a supporting force while he himself led eight hundred horsemen to fight in the van.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent his son Wudie with two hundred eighty horsemen as a reserve while he personally led eight hundred cavalry into the front fight.

sentences.zh: 連射六十餘人，皆應弦而斃，宋兵遂奔潰。

translations.literal: He shot down more than sixty men in succession, all of whom fell the moment the arrow struck; the Song army then broke and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He shot down more than sixty men in a row, each falling the instant the arrow struck, and the Song army broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲觀水戰，使世傑領水軍百人試之。

translations.literal: Hailing wished to observe naval combat and had Shijie lead one hundred sailors in a trial engagement.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing wanted to see a naval engagement and had Shijie lead one hundred sailors in a trial fight.

sentences.zh: 宋人舟大而多，世傑舟小，乃急進，至中流取勝而還。

translations.literal: Song boats were large and numerous; Shijie's boats were small, yet he pressed forward urgently, reached midstream, gained victory, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Song boats were large and numerous, while Shijie's were small. Even so he pressed forward hard, fought to midstream, won, and returned.

sentences.zh: 大定初，世傑複取陝州，敗宋兵石壕鎮，複敗宋援兵三千人，遂圍陝州。

translations.literal: Early in Dading, Shijie again took Shanzhou, defeated Song troops at Shihao Fort, again defeated three thousand Song reinforcements, and then besieged Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era Shijie retook Shanzhou, defeated Song forces at Shihao Fort, routed three thousand Song reinforcements, and then laid siege to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋兵二千自潼關來，世傑以兵二百四十迎擊之，射殺十余人，宋兵敗走。

translations.literal: Two thousand Song troops came from Tong Pass; Shijie with two hundred forty men met and attacked them, shot down more than ten, and the Song troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Song troops came from Tong Pass. Shijie met them with two hundred forty men, shot down more than ten, and put the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 複敗之於土壕山，生擒一將。

translations.literal: He again defeated them at Tuhao Mountain and took one general alive.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Tuhao Mountain and captured a general alive.

sentences.zh: 複以兵三百至斗門城，遇宋兵萬余，宋將三人挺槍來刺世傑，世傑以刀斷其鎗，宋兵乃退。

translations.literal: Again with three hundred men he reached Doumen City and encountered more than ten thousand Song troops; three Song generals thrust their spears to stab Shijie, but Shijie severed their spears with his sword, and the Song troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: With three hundred men he reached Doumen City and ran into more than ten thousand Song troops. Three Song generals thrust their spears at him, but Shijie cut the spearheads off with his sword, and the Song force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 複以四謀克軍敗宋兵于土華，複圍陝州。

translations.literal: Again with four meng'an units he defeated Song troops at Tuhua and again besieged Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With four meng'an units he defeated Song forces at Tuhua and once again besieged Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 世傑嘗擐甲佩刀，腰箭百隻，持鎗躍馬，往來軍中。

translations.literal: Shijie would sometimes don armor, gird on his sword, carry a hundred arrows at his waist, seize a spear and leap on his horse, and ride back and forth through the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie would sometimes ride through the camp in full armor, sword at his side and a hundred arrows at his belt, spear in hand — a startling figure on horseback.

sentences.zh: 敵人見而異之，曰：「真神將也。」

translations.literal: The enemy who saw him marveled, saying: "A true divine general."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy who saw him were awestruck. "A true god of war," they said.

sentences.zh: 親率選卒二百餘人穴地以入，城遂拔。

translations.literal: He personally led more than two hundred picked soldiers who tunneled into the city; the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led more than two hundred picked soldiers who tunneled into the city, and Shanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 再破宋軍三萬人，複虢州。

translations.literal: He again broke thirty thousand Song troops and recovered Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He routed another Song army of thirty thousand and retook Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為衛州防禦使，改河南路統軍都監。

translations.literal: Before long he became defender of Wei Prefecture and was changed to overall military supervisor of the Henan Route.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made defender of Wei Prefecture, then overall military supervisor of the Henan Route.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，上慰勞良久，除西北路副統，賜廄馬、弓矢、佩刀。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, the emperor comforted and rewarded him at length, made him deputy commander of the Northwest Route, and granted him an imperial stable horse, bow and arrows, and a girdle sword.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was comforted and rewarded at length by the emperor, appointed deputy commander of the Northwest Route, and given an imperial stable horse, bow and arrows, and a girdle sword.

sentences.zh: 從僕散忠義討契丹。

translations.literal: He followed Pusan Zhongyi in campaigning against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pusan Zhongyi in the campaign against the Khitan rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改華州防禦使，與徒單合喜經略隴右。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was changed to defender of Hua Prefecture and with Tushan Hexi administered Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed he was made defender of Hua Prefecture and, together with Tushan Hexi, administered Longyou.

sentences.zh: 合喜複德順，至東山堡，宋兵捍絕樵路，世傑擊走之，追至城下。
