translations.literal: Hexi recovered Deshun; reaching Dongshan Fort, Song troops blocked the firewood-gathering routes; Shijie attacked and drove them off, pursuing to beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi retook Deshun. At Dongshan Fort, Song troops had cut off the firewood routes. Shijie attacked and drove them off, pursuing them to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城中出兵約二萬餘，敗之，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The city sent out about twenty thousand troops; he defeated them, killing and wounding a great many.
translations.idiomatic: The city sent out some twenty thousand troops. He defeated them, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 宋經略使荊皋棄德順走，世傑與左都監璋追破其軍。

translations.literal: Song frontier commissioner Jing Gao abandoned Deshun and fled; Shijie with Left Overall Supervisor Zhang pursued and broke his army.
translations.idiomatic: Song frontier commissioner Jing Gao abandoned Deshun and fled. Shijie and Left Overall Supervisor Zhang pursued and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 改亳州防禦使，四遷通遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to defender of Bo Prefecture and after four promotions became military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defender of Bo Prefecture and, after four further promotions, became military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 宋人輒入鞏州境糶米麵，有司執之，世傑署案作歸附人，縱遣之。

translations.literal: Song men repeatedly entered Gong Prefecture territory to sell rice and flour; officials seized them, but Shijie annotated the cases as surrendered subjects and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Song subjects kept crossing into Gong Prefecture to sell grain and flour. When officials arrested them, Shijie marked the cases as involving surrendered subjects and set them free.

sentences.zh: 譯吏蔡松壽誣府主謀叛，坐斬。

translations.literal: The translator clerk Cai Songsou falsely accused the prefect of plotting rebellion; for this he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The translator clerk Cai Songsou falsely accused the prefect of plotting rebellion and was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起為弘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recalled as prefect of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Dading he was recalled to serve as prefect of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 累遷亳州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became defender of Bo Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose again to defender of Bo Prefecture and died in office.

sentences.zh: 世傑少貧，然疏財尚氣，每臨陣，敵眾既敗，必戒士卒毋縱殺掠。

translations.literal: Shijie was poor in youth, yet he spread his wealth and prized honor; whenever he faced battle, once the enemy masses were defeated he always admonished his soldiers not to indulge in slaughter and pillage.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie had been poor in youth, yet he was generous and high-minded. In every battle, once the enemy was broken, he always forbade his men from slaughter and looting.

sentences.zh: 平居非忠孝不言，親賢樂善，甚獲當世之譽雲。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he spoke of nothing that was not loyalty or filial piety; he honored the worthy and delighted in good deeds, and won great praise from his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he spoke only of loyalty and filial piety, honored the worthy, and delighted in good deeds, and he won wide praise in his own day.

sentences.zh: 蕭懷忠

translations.literal: Xiao Huaizhong
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huaizhong

sentences.zh: 蕭懷忠，本名好胡，奚人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Huaizhong, original name Haohu, was a Xi man.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huaizhong, whose original name was Haohu, was a man of the Xi people.

sentences.zh: 為西北路招討使。

translations.literal: He served as pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: He served as pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route.

sentences.zh: 蕭裕等謀立遼後，使蕭招折往西北路結懷忠，並結節度使耶律朗為助。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu and others plotted to establish a Liao heir and sent Xiao Zhaozhe to the Northwest Route to win over Huaizhong, and also to win the military commissioner Yelü Lang as ally.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu and others plotted to set up a Liao heir. They sent Xiao Zhaozhe to the Northwest Route to win over Huaizhong and also to secure the aid of military commissioner Yelü Lang.

sentences.zh: 懷忠與朗有隙，遂執招折並執朗，遣使上變。

translations.literal: Huaizhong had a rift with Lang, so he seized Zhaozhe and also seized Lang, and sent envoys to report the conspiracy to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong was at odds with Lang, so he arrested Zhaozhe and Lang alike and sent envoys to report the plot to the throne.

sentences.zh: 裕等既誅，懷忠為樞密副使，賜今名。

translations.literal: After Yu and the others were executed, Huaizhong was made deputy privy councilor and granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu and his co-conspirators were executed, Huaizhong was made deputy privy councilor and granted the name he now bore.

sentences.zh: 複為西北路招討使，西京留守，封王。

translations.literal: He again became pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route, Western Capital military governor, and was enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: He again became pacification commissioner of the Northwest Route and military governor of the Western Capital, and was enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 改南京留守。

translations.literal: He was changed to Southern Capital military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 契丹撒八反，複以懷忠為西京留宋、西南面兵馬都統，與樞密使僕散思恭、北京留守蕭賾、右衛將軍蕭禿剌、護衛十人長斡盧保往討之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Sa Ba rebelled, Huaizhong was again made Western Capital military governor and overall commander of southwestern forces, and with Privy Councillor Pusan Sigong, Northern Capital military governor Xiao Ze, Right Guard General Xiao Tula, and Guards Ten-Captain Wolubao went to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Sa Ba rose in revolt, Huaizhong was again appointed Western Capital military governor and overall commander of the southwestern forces. With Privy Councillor Pusan Sigong, Northern Capital military governor Xiao Ze, Right Guard General Xiao Tula, and Guards Ten-Captain Wolubao, he marched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 蕭禿剌戰無功，大軍追撒八不及。

translations.literal: Xiao Tula fought without success; the main army pursued Sa Ba but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tula fought without success, and though the main army pursued Sa Ba, it could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 而海陵意謂懷忠與蕭裕皆契丹人，本同謀，逾年乃執招折上變，而撒八亦契丹部族，恐其合，以師恭與太后密語，而禿剌無功，懷忠、賾、師恭逸賊，既殺師恭，族滅其家，使使即軍中殺賾、懷忠，皆族之。

translations.literal: Hailing thought that because Huaizhong and Xiao Yu were both Khitan they had originally conspired together, and that only after more than a year did Huaizhong seize Zhaozhe and report the plot; Sa Ba was also of the Khitan tribes, and Hailing feared they might unite. Because Sigong had held secret conversations with the empress dowager, and Tula had achieved nothing, and Huaizhong, Ze, and Sigong had let the rebel escape — after Sigong was already killed and his clan exterminated, he sent envoys to execute Ze and Huaizhong in camp; all were subjected to clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing suspected that Huaizhong and Xiao Yu, both Khitan, had originally been co-conspirators, and that Huaizhong had waited more than a year before arresting Zhaozhe and reporting the plot. Sa Ba was also Khitan, and Hailing feared they might join forces. Sigong had held secret talks with the empress dowager, Tula had achieved nothing, and Huaizhong, Ze, and Sigong had all let the rebel escape. After Sigong was killed and his clan wiped out, Hailing sent envoys to execute Ze and Huaizhong in camp, and their clans were exterminated as well.

sentences.zh: 斡盧保、禿剌初為罪首，但誅之而已。

translations.literal: Wolubao and Tula had originally been the chief culprits, but they were simply executed and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Wolubao and Tula had originally been the chief culprits, but they were simply executed without extending punishment to their clans.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，追複賾、懷忠、禿剌、斡盧保官爵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading, the offices and ranks of Ze, Huaizhong, Tula, and Wolubao were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 the offices and ranks of Ze, Huaizhong, Tula, and Wolubao were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 賾弟安州刺史頤求襲賾之謀克，上不許謀克，而以賾家產付之。

translations.literal: Ze's younger brother Yi, prefect of An Prefecture, sought to inherit Ze's meng'an office; the emperor did not permit the meng'an post but entrusted Ze's household property to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's younger brother Yi, prefect of An Prefecture, asked to inherit Ze's meng'an office. The emperor denied the meng'an post but entrusted Ze's household property to him.

sentences.zh: 移剌按答

translations.literal: Yila Anda
translations.idiomatic: Yila Anda

sentences.zh: 移剌按答，遼橫帳人也。

translations.literal: Yila Anda was of the Liao Horizontal Tab branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Anda was of the Liao Horizontal Tab branch.

sentences.zh: 父留斡，與耶律餘睹俱來降。

translations.literal: His father Liugan came and surrendered together with Yelü Yudu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liugan came over and surrendered together with Yelü Yudu.

sentences.zh: 西京下，複叛，留斡遇害，按答以死事之子，授左奉宸。

translations.literal: When the Western Capital fell, Liugan rebelled again and was killed; as the son of a man who died in service, Anda was appointed Left Fengchen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Capital fell, Liugan rebelled again and was killed. As the son of a man who had died in service, Anda was appointed Left Fengchen.

sentences.zh: 熙宗初，充護衛，除安州刺史，累官東京副留守。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xizong's reign he served in the imperial guard, was made prefect of An Prefecture, and through successive posts reached deputy military governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xizong's reign he entered the imperial guard, became prefect of An Prefecture, and rose through successive posts to deputy military governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 參知政事完顏守道經略北方，攝咸平路屯軍都統。

translations.literal: When Associate Councilor Wanyan Shoudao administered the north, Anda served as acting overall commander of garrison troops on the Xianping Route.
translations.idiomatic: When Associate Councilor Wanyan Shoudao took charge of the northern frontier, Anda served as acting overall commander of garrison troops on the Xianping Route.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部侍郎，徙西北、西南兩路舊設堡戍迫近內地者于極邊安置，仍與泰州、臨潢邊堡相接。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice minister of war, relocated fortresses and garrisons of the Northwest and Southwest routes that had long been established near the interior to the outermost frontier, and linked them with the border forts of Taizhou and Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice minister of war and relocated the Northwest and Southwest route fortresses and garrisons that had been placed too close to the interior, resettling them on the outermost frontier and linking them with the border forts of Taizhou and Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 除武定軍節度使，以招徠邊部功遷東北路招討使，改臨潢尹，卒。

translations.literal: He was made military commissioner of the Wuding Army; for achievements in winning over frontier tribes he was promoted to pacification commissioner of the Northeast Route, changed to prefect of Linhuang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Wuding Army. For his success in winning over frontier tribes he was promoted to pacification commissioner of the Northeast Route, then made prefect of Linhuang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 按答騎射絕倫，善相馬，嘗論及善射者，世宗曰：「能如卿乎？」

translations.literal: Anda's mounted archery was peerless and he was skilled at judging horses. Once when discussion turned to expert archers, Emperor Shizong said: "Can anyone match you?"
translations.idiomatic: Anda's horsemanship and archery were unmatched, and he had a gift for judging horses. Once, when the talk turned to fine archers, Emperor Shizong asked: "Is there anyone who can match you?"

sentences.zh: 閱馬於市，見良馬，雖羸瘦，輒與善價取之，他日果良馬也。

translations.literal: Inspecting horses in the market, whenever he saw a fine horse, even if it was thin and weak, he would pay a good price to take it; later it indeed proved to be a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the horse market he would pay a good price for any fine horse he spotted, even if it was gaunt and poor-looking — and it would invariably prove to be a fine steed.

sentences.zh: 孛朮魯阿魯罕

translations.literal: Beipailu Aruhan
translations.idiomatic: Beipailu Aruhan

sentences.zh: 孛朮魯阿魯罕，隆州琶離葛山人。

translations.literal: Beipailu Aruhan was a man of Palige Mountain in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Beipailu Aruhan was from Palige Mountain in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，選習契丹字，再選習女直字。

translations.literal: At eight he was selected to study Khitan script; selected again to study Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was chosen to study Khitan script, and later selected again to study Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 既壯，為黃龍府路萬戶令史。

translations.literal: When grown, he served as a clerk of the wanhu office on the Huanglongfu Route.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he served as a clerk in the wanhu office on the Huanglongfu Route.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，試外路胥吏三百人補隨朝，阿魯罕在第一，補宗正府令史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengyuan, three hundred clerks from outer routes were examined for appointment at court; Aruhan placed first and was appointed clerk of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengyuan 2 three hundred clerks from the outer circuits were examined for appointment at court. Aruhan placed first and was appointed clerk of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 累擢尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He was promoted through successive posts to clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義討窩斡，辟置幕府，掌邊關文字，甚見信任。

translations.literal: When Pusan Zhongyi campaigned against Wowo, he recruited Aruhan to his staff to manage frontier correspondence and trusted him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Pusan Zhongyi campaigned against Wowo, he recruited Aruhan to his staff to handle frontier correspondence and came to trust him deeply.

sentences.zh: 窩斡既平，阿魯罕招集散亡，複業者數萬人。

translations.literal: After Wowo was pacified, Aruhan gathered the scattered and destitute; tens of thousands returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: After Wowo was suppressed, Aruhan gathered the scattered and destitute, and tens of thousands returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 複從忠義伐宋，屢入奏事，論列可否。

translations.literal: He again followed Zhongyi in attacking Song, repeatedly entering court to report and arguing what should or should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zhongyi against Song, repeatedly reporting to court and arguing what should and should not be done.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「阿魯罕所言，可行者即行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers: "Whatever Aruhan proposes that can be put into practice should be implemented at once."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Whatever Aruhan proposes that can be done, do it at once."

sentences.zh: 宋人請和，忠義使阿魯罕往。

translations.literal: When the Song sought peace, Zhongyi sent Aruhan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song sought peace, Zhongyi sent Aruhan to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 和議定，阿魯罕入奏，賜銀百兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: When the peace terms were settled, Aruhan reported to court and was given one hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the peace terms were settled, Aruhan reported to court and was rewarded with one hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.

sentences.zh: 忠義薦阿魯罕有才幹，可任尚書省都事，詔以為大理司直。

translations.literal: Zhongyi recommended Aruhan as capable and fit for chief secretary of the Secretariat; an edict made him direct clerk of the Court of Judgment Review.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi recommended Aruhan as talented and fit to serve as chief secretary of the Secretariat. An edict appointed him direct clerk of the Court of Judgment Review.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授尚書省都事，除同知順天軍節度事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed chief secretary of the Secretariat and vice commissioner of the Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed chief secretary of the Secretariat and vice commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈志寧北巡，阿魯罕攝左右司郎中。

translations.literal: When He Shilie Zhining toured the north, Aruhan served as acting director of the Left and Right Bureau of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When He Shilie Zhining toured the north, Aruhan served as acting director of the Left and Right Bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除刑部員外郎，再遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was made vice director of the Ministry of Punishments and promoted again to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made vice director of the Ministry of Punishments and then promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 上問紇石烈良弼曰：「阿魯罕何如人也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked He Shilie Liangbi: "What sort of man is Aruhan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He Shilie Liangbi: "What kind of man is Aruhan?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「有幹材，持心忠正，出言不阿順。」

translations.literal: He replied: "He has administrative talent, a loyal and upright heart, and when he speaks he does not flatter."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi answered: "He is capable, upright at heart, and does not speak to flatter."

sentences.zh: 數日，遷勸農副使，兼同修國史，侍御史如故。

translations.literal: A few days later he was promoted to vice commissioner for agriculture and concurrently editor of the national history, retaining his post as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was promoted to vice commissioner for agriculture and concurrent editor of the national history, while retaining his post as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 改右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to director of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 奏請徙河南戍軍屯營城中者於十裏外，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that garrison troops of the Henan Route encamped within cities be moved ten li outside; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Henan garrison troops encamped inside city walls should be moved ten li outside, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，附山東統軍都監，徙置河南八猛安。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, attached as overall military supervisor of the Shandong Route, and relocated eight meng'an of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, attached as overall military supervisor of the Shandong Route, and resettled eight Henan meng'an.

sentences.zh: 遷武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，改西南路招討使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel and was reassigned as pacification commissioner of the Southwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel, then reassigned as pacification commissioner of the Southwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 有司督本路猛安人戶所貸官粟，阿魯罕乞俟豐年，從之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices pressed the meng'an households of this route to repay official grain they had borrowed; Aruhan requested that collection wait until a good harvest year, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities pressed meng'an households on the route to repay official grain they had borrowed, Aruhan asked that collection be deferred until a bumper harvest, and his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 軍人有以甲葉貿易諸物，天德榷場及界外歲采銅礦，或因私挾兵鐵與之市易，皆一切禁絕之。

translations.literal: Soldiers traded armor plates for various goods; at the Tiande monopoly mart and in yearly copper mining beyond the border, some privately carried weapons and iron to trade with them—all of this he completely prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly forbade soldiers from trading armor plates for goods, and he shut down all private traffic in weapons and iron at the Tiande monopoly market and at the annual copper mines beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上番軍不許用親戚、奴婢及傭雇者，營塹損圮以時葺治，不與所部猛安謀克會宴，故兵民皆畏愛之。

translations.literal: Regular garrison troops were not permitted to use relatives, slaves, or hired laborers; damaged encampments and ramparts were repaired on schedule; he did not hold banquets with the meng'an and moke under his command—therefore both soldiers and civilians feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade garrison troops on rotation from using relatives, slaves, or hired hands; he saw that damaged camps and ramparts were repaired on time; and he refused to hold banquets with the meng'an and moke under his command. For these reasons both soldiers and civilians respected and admired him.

sentences.zh: 上謂太尉守道曰：「阿魯罕及上京留守完顏烏裏也皆起身胥吏，阿魯罕為人沉厚，其賢過之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Grand Marshal Shoudao: "Aruhan and the Shangjing defender Wanyan Wuliye both rose from minor clerks; Aruhan is a man of deep steadiness, and in virtue he surpasses Wuliye."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Grand Marshal Shoudao: "Aruhan and the Shangjing defender Wanyan Wuliye both started out as petty clerks, but Aruhan is a man of deep steadiness, and in talent he surpasses Wuliye."

sentences.zh: 改陝西路統軍使兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to military commissioner of the Shaanxi Route while also serving as prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to military commissioner of the Shaanxi Route and concurrently appointed prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 陝西軍籍有闕，舊例用子弟補充，而材多不堪用，阿魯罕于阿裏喜旗鼓手內選補。

translations.literal: There were vacancies in the Shaanxi military rolls; by old practice sons and younger brothers were used to fill them, but most lacked the ability; Aruhan selected replacements from among the drum-and-banner troops of Alixi.
translations.idiomatic: When vacancies opened in the Shaanxi military rolls, the old practice was to fill them with sons and younger brothers, but most proved unfit; Aruhan instead selected replacements from the drum-and-banner troops of Alixi.

sentences.zh: 軍人以春牧馬，經夏不收飼，瘠弱多死，阿魯罕命以時收秣之，故死損者少。

translations.literal: Soldiers pastured horses in spring but did not bring them in for feeding through summer, so many grew emaciated and died; Aruhan ordered that they be brought in and foddered on schedule, and deaths were therefore fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers pastured horses in spring but often left them out all summer without bringing them in to feed, so many grew thin and died; Aruhan ordered the horses brought in and fed on schedule, and losses fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 仍春秋督閱軍士騎射，以嚴武備。

translations.literal: He also supervised the cavalry archery of the troops in spring and autumn to tighten military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: He also inspected the troops' mounted archery every spring and autumn to keep military readiness strict.

sentences.zh: 終南采漆者，節其期限，檢其出入，以防奸細。

translations.literal: For those gathering lacquer in the Zhongnan Mountains, he set limits on their periods of work and inspected their coming and going to guard against spies.
translations.idiomatic: For lacquer gatherers working in the Zhongnan Mountains, he set time limits and checked their movements in and out to guard against spies.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「阿魯罕所至稱治，陝西政績尤著，用之雖遲，亦可得數年力也。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Wherever Aruhan has gone he has been praised for good governance; his achievements in Shaanxi are especially notable. Though we employ him late, we can still gain several years of service from him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Wherever Aruhan has served, people praise his governance, and his record in Shaanxi is especially strong. Even if we use him late, we can still get several good years out of him."

sentences.zh: 召為參知政事，命條上天德、陝西行事，上稱善。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice grand councilor and ordered to submit in detail an account of his actions at Tiande and in Shaanxi; the emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Aruhan was summoned as vice grand councilor and ordered to submit a detailed report on his work at Tiande and in Shaanxi; the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞致仕，除北京留守，卒。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of illness, was appointed defender of the Northern Capital, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire because of illness, was appointed defender of the Northern Capital, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《記》曰：「君子聽磬聲，則思死封疆之臣。」

translations.literal: Commentary: The Record says: "When a gentleman hears the sound of stone chimes, he thinks of ministers who died defending the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Record of Rites says: "When a gentleman hears the sound of stone chimes, he thinks of the ministers who died defending the frontier."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「疆埸之事，慎守其一而備其不虞。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "In matters of the border, vigilantly hold what you have and guard against the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Zhuan says: "In frontier affairs, hold what you have with care and prepare against the unforeseen."

sentences.zh: 故守戍邊圉之臣，不可以不論焉。

translations.literal: Therefore ministers who garrison and defend the frontiers cannot be passed over without discussion.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, ministers who garrison and defend the frontier cannot be left out of account.

sentences.zh: 趙興祥

translations.literal: Zhao Xingxiang
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingxiang

sentences.zh: 趙興祥，平州盧龍人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingxiang was a man of Lulong in Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingxiang was a native of Lulong in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六世祖思溫，遼燕京留守，封天水郡王。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Siwen was defender of Yanjing under Liao and was enfeoffed as Prince of the Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Siwen had served as defender of Yanjing under the Liao and was enfeoffed as Prince of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父瑾，遼靜江軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Jin was military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army under Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had been military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army under the Liao.

sentences.zh: 興祥以父任閣門祗候，謁告省親于白霫。

translations.literal: Xingxiang, through his father's position, became a gate usher and requested leave to visit his family at Bai Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's influence, Xingxiang became a gate usher and requested leave to visit his family at Bai Xi.

sentences.zh: 會遼季土賊據郡作亂，興祥攜母及弟妹奔燕京，不能進，乃自柳城涉砂磧，夜視星斗而行。

translations.literal: It happened that local bandits seized the commandery in the final years of Liao and rebelled; Xingxiang fled with his mother and younger siblings toward Yanjing but could not get through, so from Liucheng they crossed sandy wastes, traveling by night guided by the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Just then, in the dying days of the Liao, local bandits seized the commandery and rose in rebellion. Xingxiang fled with his mother and younger siblings toward Yanjing but could not get through, so from Liucheng they crossed the sandy wastes, traveling by night under the stars.

sentences.zh: 僅達遼軍，而不知遼主所向，遂還柳城。

translations.literal: They barely reached Liao troops but did not know where the Liao emperor had gone, so they returned to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: They barely reached Liao forces but did not know where the Liao emperor had gone, so they turned back to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 及婁室獲遼主，興祥乃歸國，從宗望伐宋，為六宅使。

translations.literal: When Niansilie captured the Liao emperor, Xingxiang then submitted to the state; he followed Zongwang in the campaign against Song and served as envoy of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: After Niansilie captured the Liao emperor, Xingxiang submitted to the Jin and followed Zongwang in the campaign against Song, serving as envoy of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，累官同知宣徽院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he rose through offices to vice director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianjuan era he rose through successive posts to vice director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 熙宗素聞興祥孝行，及英悼太子受冊，以本官起複，護視太子。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong had long heard of Xingxiang's filial conduct; when Prince Yingdao received investiture, Xingxiang was recalled from mourning in his former post to attend and guard the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong had long known of Xingxiang's filial conduct, and when Prince Yingdao was invested as heir, Xingxiang was recalled from mourning in his former post to attend and guard the prince.

sentences.zh: 轉右宣徽使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 天德初，改左宣徽使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was changed to left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiande era he was made left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗問興祥，欲使子弟為官，當自言。

translations.literal: Hailing once asked Xingxiang whether, if he wished to have his sons or younger brothers given office, he should speak up himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once asked Xingxiang whether, if he wanted his sons or younger brothers given office, he should say so himself.

sentences.zh: 興祥辭謝。

translations.literal: Xingxiang declined with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxiang politely declined.

sentences.zh: 海陵善之，賜以玉帶，詔曰：「汝官雖未至一品，可佩此侍立。」

translations.literal: Hailing approved of this, granted him a jade belt, and issued an edict: "Though your rank has not yet reached the first grade, you may wear this and stand in attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing approved and granted him a jade belt, issuing an edict: "Though your rank has not yet reached the first grade, you may wear this and stand in attendance."

sentences.zh: 為濟南尹，賜車馬、金幣、金銀器皿，改絳陽軍節度使，召為太子少保，封廣平郡王，改封钜鹿。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Jinan, given carriages, horses, gold coin, and gold and silver vessels, transferred to military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army, summoned as junior guardian of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Prince of the Guangping Commandery, and then re-enfeoffed as Prince of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jinan and given carriages, horses, gold, and gold and silver vessels; then he was transferred to military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army, recalled as junior guardian of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping, and later re-enfeoffed as Prince of Julu.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，例奪王爵，遷太子少傅，封申國公，起為定武軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong, by regulation his princely title was removed; he was transferred to junior tutor of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, and recalled to serve as military commissioner of the Dingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenglong era, his princely title was removed by regulation; he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Shen, and recalled to serve as military commissioner of the Dingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，興祥二子從軍。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, two of Xingxiang's sons joined the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing campaigned against Song, two of Xingxiang's sons went with the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，海陵尚在淮南，二子未得還。

translations.literal: When Shizong came to the throne, Hailing was still south of the Huai, and the two sons could not yet return.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne, Hailing was still south of the Huai, and the two sons had not yet been able to return.

sentences.zh: 興祥來見於平州，世宗嘉其誠款，以為秘書監，複為左宣徽使。

translations.literal: Xingxiang came to see Shizong at Pingzhou; Shizong praised his sincere loyalty and made him director of the Secretariat, restoring him as left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxiang came to see Shizong at Pingzhou; Shizong praised his sincere loyalty, made him director of the Secretariat, and restored him as left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「尚食庖人猥多，徒費廩祿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The cooks of the imperial kitchen are excessively numerous and waste grain salaries for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "There are far too many imperial kitchen cooks, and they waste grain salaries for nothing.

sentences.zh: 朕在籓邸時，家務皆委執事者，自即位以來，事皆留心。

translations.literal: When I was in the princely residence, household affairs were all entrusted to stewards; since ascending the throne I have attended to everything myself.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the princely residence, I left household affairs to my stewards, but since taking the throne I have attended to everything myself.

sentences.zh: 俸祿出於百姓，不可妄費，庖人可約量損減。」

translations.literal: Salaries come from the people and must not be squandered; the number of cooks can be reduced by measured steps."
translations.idiomatic: Salaries come from the people and must not be wasted; the number of cooks should be reduced accordingly."

sentences.zh: 近臣獻琵琶，世宗卻之，謂興祥曰：「朕憂勞天下，未嘗以聲伎為心，自今勿複有獻，宜悉諭朕意。」

translations.literal: A close attendant offered a pipa; Shizong refused it and said to Xingxiang: "I toil in care for the empire and have never taken music and performance to heart; from now on there must be no more such gifts—you should make my intent fully known."
translations.idiomatic: A close attendant offered a pipa, but Shizong refused it and said to Xingxiang: "I labor in care for the empire and have never cared for music and entertainments. From now on there must be no more such gifts—you should make my wishes fully known."

sentences.zh: 有司奏南北邊事未息，恐財用未給，乞罷修神龍殿涼位工役。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported that northern and southern frontier matters had not yet settled and feared revenue would be insufficient; they requested suspension of work on the cool chambers of the Divine Dragon Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported that affairs on the northern and southern frontiers were still unsettled and feared that funds would fall short, and they asked that work on the cool chambers of the Divine Dragon Hall be halted.

sentences.zh: 上即日使興祥傳詔罷之。

translations.literal: That same day the emperor had Xingxiang convey an edict halting it.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor had Xingxiang convey an edict halting the project.

sentences.zh: 久之，以其孫珣為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: After some time, his grandson Xun was appointed gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, his grandson Xun was appointed gate usher.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上幸安州春水，召興祥赴萬春節。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Anzhou for the spring hunt and summoned Xingxiang to the Ten Thousand Spring Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor went to Anzhou for the spring hunt and summoned Xingxiang to the Ten Thousand Spring Festival.

sentences.zh: 上謁於良鄉，賜銀五百兩，感風眩，賜醫藥。

translations.literal: The emperor received him at Liangxiang and granted him five hundred taels of silver; feeling dizzy from wind ailment, Xingxiang was given medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him at Liangxiang and granted him five hundred taels of silver; when Xingxiang suffered dizziness from wind ailment, the emperor also gave him medicine.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 石抹榮

translations.literal: Shi Morong
translations.idiomatic: Shi Morong

sentences.zh: 石抹榮，字昌祖。

translations.literal: Shi Morong, courtesy name Changzu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Morong, courtesy name Changzu.

sentences.zh: 七世祖仕遼，封順國王。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor served Liao and was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunguo.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor had served the Liao and was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunguo.

sentences.zh: 遼主奔天德，榮父惕益挺身赴之。

translations.literal: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Rong's father Tieyi went forth personally to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Rong's father Tieyi went in person to join him.

sentences.zh: 是時，榮方六歲，母忽土特滿攜之流離道路，宗室穀神得之，納為次室，榮就養于穀神家。

translations.literal: At that time Rong was only six; his mother Huteteman took him and fled along the roads; the imperial clansman Gushen found them, took her as a secondary consort, and Rong was raised in Gushen's household.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Rong was only six; his mother Huteteman took him and wandered the roads in exile. The imperial clansman Gushen found them, took her as a secondary consort, and Rong was raised in Gushen's household.

sentences.zh: 惕益既見遼主，委以軍事。

translations.literal: After Tieyi reached the Liao emperor, military affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Tieyi reached the Liao emperor, military affairs were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 軍敗被執，將殺之，金源郡王銀朮可曰：「彼忠於所事，殺之何以勸後。」

translations.literal: His army was defeated and he was captured; they were about to execute him when Prince of Jinyuan Yinzhuke said: "He was loyal to whom he served—if we kill him, how shall we encourage those who follow?"
translations.idiomatic: His army was defeated and he was captured; they were about to execute him when Prince of Jinyuan Yinzhuke said: "He was loyal to the master he served—if we kill him, how will we encourage those who come after?"

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。

translations.literal: So he was released.
translations.idiomatic: So he was released.

sentences.zh: 後從伐宋，卒於軍中。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Song and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the campaign against Song and died in the army.

sentences.zh: 榮年長，事秦王宗翰，居幕府。

translations.literal: When Rong grew up he served Prince Qin Zonghan and lived in the staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong came of age he served Prince Qin Zonghan and lived on his staff.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，充護衛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he served in the guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianjuan era he served in the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 熙宗宴飲，命胙王元與榮角力，榮勝之，連僕力士六七人。

translations.literal: At a banquet Emperor Xizong ordered Prince Zuo Yuan to wrestle with Rong; Rong defeated him and threw down six or seven strongmen in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Emperor Xizong ordered Prince Zuo Yuan to wrestle with Rong; Rong won and threw down six or seven strongmen in succession.

sentences.zh: 熙宗親飲之酒，賜以金幣，遷宿直將軍。

translations.literal: Xizong personally gave him wine, granted him gold coin, and promoted him to night-duty general.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong personally gave him wine, granted him gold, and promoted him to night-duty general.

sentences.zh: 天德初，除開遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was appointed military commissioner of the Kaiyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiande era he was appointed military commissioner of the Kaiyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 入謝，不覺泣下。

translations.literal: Upon entering to give thanks he wept unawares.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered to give thanks, he wept without realizing it.

sentences.zh: 海陵問其故。

translations.literal: Hailing asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked why.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「老母在穀神家，違去膝下，是以感泣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "My old mother is in Gushen's household; leaving her side, I am moved to tears."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "My old mother is in Gushen's household, and leaving her side moves me to tears."

sentences.zh: 乃詔其母與之俱行，仍賜錢萬貫。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued for his mother to travel with him, and ten thousand strings of cash were granted besides.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued for his mother to travel with him, and he was also granted ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 改天德尹，徙泰寧軍，再除延安、東平尹。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Tiande, transferred to Taining Army, and then successively appointed prefect of Yan'an and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Tiande, transferred to Taining, and then successively appointed prefect of Yan'an and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 海陵南征，為神果軍都總管，留駐泗州，以遏逋卒。

translations.literal: When Hailing marched south he became overall commander of the Shengou Army, remaining garrisoned at Sizhou to check deserters.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing marched south, Morong became overall commander of the Shengou Army and remained garrisoned at Sizhou to block fleeing soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大定初，還鎮東平，與戶部尚書梁钅求按治山東盜賊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he returned to command at Dongping and, together with Liang Qiu, director of the Ministry of Revenue, investigated and suppressed bandits in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dading era he returned to command at Dongping and, together with Liang Qiu, director of the Ministry of Revenue, investigated and suppressed bandits in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二年，以本官充山東東西、大名等路都統。

translations.literal: In the second year, retaining his office, he served as overall commander of the eastern and western Shandong routes, Daming, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, while retaining his post, he served as overall commander of eastern and western Shandong, Daming, and other routes.

sentences.zh: 有疾，改太原尹，徙益都尹。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he was made prefect of Taiyuan, then transferred to prefect of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he was made prefect of Taiyuan, then transferred to prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複召為簽書樞密院事，北京、東京留守，陝西路統軍使，南京、西京留守。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning as deputy director of the Privy Council, defender of the Northern and Eastern capitals, military commissioner of the Shaanxi Route, and defender of the Southern and Western capitals.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning and successively served as deputy director of the Privy Council, defender of the Northern and Eastern capitals, military commissioner of the Shaanxi Route, and defender of the Southern and Western capitals.

sentences.zh: 榮與河南尹婁室、陝州防禦使石抹靳家奴皆坐高賈賣私物、抑賈買民物得罪。

translations.literal: Rong, together with Lou Shi, prefect of Henan, and Shi Mo Qinjianu, defense commissioner of Shanzhou, were all convicted for selling private goods at high prices and forcing the people to sell goods at low prices.
translations.idiomatic: Morong, together with Lou Shi, prefect of Henan, and Shi Mo Qinjianu, defense commissioner of Shanzhou, were all convicted of selling private goods at inflated prices and forcing the people to sell their goods at low prices.

sentences.zh: 靳家奴前為單州刺史，廉察官行郡，乃劫制民使作虛譽，用是得遷同知太原尹，複多取民利。

translations.literal: Qinjianu had formerly been prefect of Shanzhou; when an integrity inspector toured the commandery, he coerced the people into giving false praise, and by this attained promotion to vice prefect of Taiyuan, again extracting many private gains from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Qinjianu had formerly been prefect of Shanzhou; when an integrity inspector toured the commandery, he coerced the people into giving false praise, and by this won promotion to vice prefect of Taiyuan, again extracting many private gains from the people.

sentences.zh: 及為陝州，尚書省奏其事，法當解職削階，上以靳家奴鼓虛聲以誑朝廷，不可恕，特詔除名。

translations.literal: When he served at Shanzhou, the Secretariat reported the matter; by law he should be removed from office and stripped of rank, but the emperor said Qinjianu had beaten empty drums to deceive the court and could not be forgiven, and specially ordered that he be expelled from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When he served at Shanzhou, the Secretariat reported the matter; by law he should have been removed from office and stripped of rank, but the emperor said Qinjianu had trumpeted false praise to deceive the court and could not be forgiven, and specially ordered that he be expelled from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 榮與婁室削兩階解職。

translations.literal: Rong and Lou Shi had two ranks stripped and were removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Morong and Lou Shi had two ranks stripped and were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，榮除臨潢尹，改臨洮尹。

translations.literal: After some time Rong was appointed prefect of Linhuang, then transferred to prefect of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Morong was appointed prefect of Linhuang, then transferred to prefect of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 敬嗣暉

translations.literal: Jing Sihui
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sihui

sentences.zh: 敬嗣暉，字唐臣，易州人。

translations.literal: Jing Sihui, courtesy name Tangchen, was a man of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sihui, courtesy name Tangchen, was a native of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 登天眷二年進士第，調懷安丞，遷弘政令，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianjuan, was assigned as assistant magistrate of Huai'an, promoted to magistrate of Hongzheng, and appointed a clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Tianjuan era, was assigned as assistant magistrate of Huai'an, promoted to magistrate of Hongzheng, and appointed a clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有才辯，海陵為宰相，愛之，及篡立，擢起居注，曆諫議大夫、吏部侍郎、左宣徽使。

translations.literal: Talented and eloquent, he was favored when Hailing served as chief minister; when Hailing usurped the throne he was promoted to diarist and successively served as grand adviser, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, and left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and eloquent, he won favor when Hailing served as chief minister; when Hailing seized the throne he was promoted to diarist and successively served as grand adviser, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, and left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年八月，尚食烹飪失宜，庖官各杖二百，嗣暉與同知宣徽院事烏居仁各杖有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Zhenyuan 3, because imperial kitchen cooking was improper, each kitchen official was beaten two hundred strokes; Sihui and Wujuren, vice director of the Palace Provisions Commission, were each beaten to differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyuan, because imperial kitchen cooking was improper, each kitchen official was beaten two hundred strokes; Sihui and Wujuren, vice director of the Palace Provisions Commission, were each beaten to differing degrees.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年伐宋，留張浩及嗣暉于南京，治尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, during the campaign against Song, Zhang Hao and Sihui were left at Nanjing to administer Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhenglong era, during the campaign against Song, Zhang Hao and Sihui were left at Nanjing to administer Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，惡嗣暉巧佞，御史大夫完顏元宜劾奏蕭玉、嗣暉、許霖等六人不可用。

translations.literal: When Shizong came to the throne he disliked Sihui's craftiness and flattery; censor-in-chief Wanyan Yuan Yi memorialized impeaching six men including Xiao Yu, Sihui, and Xu Lin as unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he disliked Sihui's craftiness and flattery; censor-in-chief Wanyan Yuan Yi memorialized impeaching six men, including Xiao Yu, Sihui, and Xu Lin, as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 嗣暉降通議大夫，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Sihui was demoted to grand master of convocation and sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui was demoted to grand master of convocation and sent back to his home district.

sentences.zh: 嗣暉練習朝儀，進止應對閒雅，由是起為丹州刺史，戒諭之曰：「卿為正隆執政，阿順取容，朕甚鄙之。

translations.literal: Sihui was practiced in court ceremony; his movements and replies were easy and refined, and for this he was recalled as prefect of Danzhou; he was admonished: "You served in government under Zhenglong, flattering to win favor—I hold that in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui was practiced in court ceremony, and his bearing and replies were easy and refined; for this he was recalled as prefect of Danzhou and admonished: "You served in government under Zhenglong, flattering to win favor, and I hold that in contempt.

sentences.zh: 今當竭力奉職，以洗前日之咎。

translations.literal: Now you must exert yourself in office to wash away your past faults.
translations.idiomatic: Now you must exert yourself in office to wash away your past faults.

sentences.zh: 苟或不悛，必罰無赦。」

translations.literal: If you do not mend your ways, punishment will be without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not mend your ways, punishment will be without mercy."

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂，起複為左宣徽使。

translations.literal: Before long, upon mourning for his mother, he was recalled from mourning as left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, after mourning for his mother, he was recalled from mourning as left director of the Palace Provisions Commission.

sentences.zh: 世宗頗好道術，謂嗣暉曰：「尚食官毋於禁中殺羊豕，朔望上七日有司毋奏刑名。」

translations.literal: Shizong was rather fond of Daoist arts and said to Sihui: "Kitchen officials must not slaughter sheep or swine within the palace; on the first and fifteenth of the month and for seven days thereafter the offices must not submit criminal cases."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was rather fond of Daoist practices and said to Sihui: "Kitchen officials must not slaughter sheep or swine within the palace, and on the first and fifteenth of the month and for seven days thereafter the offices must not submit criminal cases."

sentences.zh: 大定七年，蒲察通除肇州防禦使，上責其飾詐，因顧嗣暉曰：「如卿不可謂無才，但純實不足耳。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dading, Pucha Tong was appointed defense commissioner of Zhaozhou; the emperor rebuked him for pretense and, turning to Sihui, said: "One cannot say you lack talent, but you are insufficiently plain and sincere."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Dading era, Pucha Tong was appointed defense commissioner of Zhaozhou; the emperor rebuked him for pretense and, turning to Sihui, said: "One cannot say you lack talent, but you are not plain and sincere enough."

sentences.zh: 久之，有榜匿名書於通衢者，稱海陵舊臣不得用者有怨望心，將圖不軌。

translations.literal: After some time an anonymous placard appeared on a public thoroughfare claiming that former ministers of Hailing who were not employed harbored resentment and would plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: After some time an anonymous placard appeared on a public thoroughfare claiming that former ministers of Hailing who had not been employed harbored resentment and would plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「豈有是哉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could there be such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How could there be such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 謂嗣暉曰：「正隆時，卿為執政，今指卿以為怨望，朕極知其不然。

translations.literal: He said to Sihui: "Under Zhenglong you served in government; now you are named as one who harbors resentment—I know extremely well that this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Sihui: "Under Zhenglong you served in government, and now you are named as one who harbors resentment—I know very well that this is not so.

sentences.zh: 卿性明達能辨，但頗自炫，釣眾人之譽，所以致此媒蘖，後當改之。」

translations.literal: You are by nature clear-sighted and discriminating, but you rather show off and fish for popular praise—this is what has brought on such slander; hereafter you must change."
translations.idiomatic: You are by nature clear-sighted and discerning, but you rather show off and fish for popular praise—that is what has brought on such slander; hereafter you must change."

sentences.zh: 十年，將有事南郊，廷議嗣暉在海陵時凡宗廟禘祫輒行太常事，複拜參知政事，詔以執政冠服攝太常。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the southern suburban rites were to be performed, court discussion noted that under Hailing Sihui had regularly conducted Grand Music matters for ancestral temple di and xia sacrifices; he was again appointed vice grand councilor, and an edict ordered him to perform the Grand Music office in chief-minister regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the southern suburban rites were to be performed, court discussion noted that under Hailing Sihui had regularly handled Grand Music affairs for the ancestral temple di and xia sacrifices; he was again appointed vice grand councilor, and an edict ordered him to perform the Grand Music office in chief-minister regalia.

sentences.zh: 禮成，薨。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：趙興祥、石抹榮自拔流離艱厄中，而克有所樹立，固其識之過人，亦其所遭際致然也。

translations.literal: Commentary: Zhao Xingxiang and Shi Morong lifted themselves out of wandering hardship and distress and were able to achieve distinction—this was certainly because their insight surpassed others, but also because of the opportunities they encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhao Xingxiang and Shi Morong lifted themselves out of exile and hardship and were able to achieve distinction—this was certainly because their insight surpassed others, but also because of the opportunities they encountered.

sentences.zh: 跡世宗之卻聲伎、減庖人，仁愛若是，而其下孰不興起哉！

translations.literal: Tracing how Emperor Shizong rejected music and performers and reduced the kitchen staff—such was his benevolence—who below him would not be stirred to rise up!
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Shizong turned away musicians and performers and cut back the palace kitchens—benevolence such as that—and who among his subordinates would not be moved to do their utmost!
